definition_zh: 视力；视觉；视野；想象、眼光；幻象、景象；远见
definition_en: the ability to see; an idea of what something could be like in the future; something you imagine seeing
core_image: 一双眼睛：既能看清眼前，也能望向别人还看不见的远方
scene: 画家站在山顶，画纸上还没有任何颜色。She closed her eyes and described the city of her vision.
sceneCN: 这里 vision 是「想象中的图景、愿景」（第 4 个义项：构想中的未来图景）；句意是她闭上眼睛，描述她想象中的那座城市。先看清，再望远，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 名词：视力；视觉；视野；想象；幻象；远见

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「视觉的」，由同根形容词构成
形容词，义为「有远见的」，也可作名词指「有远见的人」
动词，义为「设想、展望」，由 en- 加同根词构成
名词，义为「电视」，由 tele-（远）加同根词构成
副词，义为「在视觉上」

senses.title: The ability to see
senses.titleCN: 视力：用眼睛感知的能力
senses.definition: the ability of the eyes to see things
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛看见东西的能力
senses.example: Her vision blurred after hours at the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 盯着屏幕几个小时后，她的视力变得模糊。
senses.why: Latin videre means to see; the noun names the very capacity of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre 意为看；这个名词指称「看」这一能力本身。

senses.title: Sight as experience
senses.titleCN: 视觉：所见之物与观看体验
senses.definition: the sense or experience of seeing, or something that is seen
senses.definitionCN: 观看这一感知方式，或被看见的东西
senses.example: The cathedral is a vision of white stone against the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大教堂是映衬在天空下的一幅白色石头的视觉景象。
senses.why: What the eye receives becomes the content of seeing; hence a striking sight.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛接收的内容就是「看」的素材，引申为引人注目的景象。

senses.title: Range of sight
senses.titleCN: 视野：目光所及的范围
senses.definition: the area that you can see from one place or position
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置能看到的空间范围
senses.example: The bird slipped out of my field of vision.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟滑出了我的视野。
senses.why: Seeing has edges; the word maps the boundary of what is visible.
senses.whyCN: 「看」有边界，这个词标出可见范围的两端。

senses.title: An imagined picture
senses.titleCN: 想象：构想中的图景或愿景
senses.definition: an idea or mental picture of what something could become
senses.definitionCN: 对某物未来样子的构想或心理图景
senses.example: She closed her eyes and described the city of her vision.
senses.exampleCN: 她闭上眼睛，描述她想象中的那座城市。
senses.why: The mind's eye sees too; an inner picture extends sight beyond the present.
senses.whyCN: 心灵的眼睛也会「看」，内心的画面把视线延伸到当下之外。

senses.title: Foresight and judgment
senses.titleCN: 远见：预见未来的眼光
senses.definition: the quality of planning or thinking wisely about the future
senses.definitionCN: 对未来做出明智规划的洞察力
senses.example: He rebuilt the school with vision and patience.
senses.exampleCN: 他以远见和耐心重建了这所学校。
senses.why: One who sees far ahead leads; imagination about the future becomes wisdom.
senses.whyCN: 能提前看见的人才能引领，对未来的想象升华为判断力。

senses.title: A dream seen as real
senses.titleCN: 幻象：梦中或恍惚间所见的景象
senses.definition: something seen in a dream or trance as if it were real
senses.definitionCN: 在梦、幻觉或宗教体验中仿佛真实看见的景象
senses.example: In the story, the prophet receives a night vision.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里，先知在夜间见到一个异象。
senses.why: An inner picture can feel as vivid as eyesight, even when asleep.
senses.whyCN: 内心的画面可以像亲眼所见一样鲜明，甚至在睡梦中。

senses.title: Clear insight
senses.titleCN: 洞察：看清本质的眼光
senses.definition: the ability to perceive clearly what is true or important
senses.definitionCN: 清楚看出真相或要点的能力
senses.example: Her memoir shows rare vision about her own past.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回忆录对自己的过去表现出罕见的洞察。
senses.why: Clear seeing turns into clear understanding; sight is a metaphor for knowing.
senses.whyCN: 看得清楚转化为想得透彻，「看」成为「懂」的隐喻。

senses.title: A haunting image
senses.titleCN: 浮现的影像：萦绕心头的画面
senses.definition: a vivid picture that appears suddenly in the mind, especially one that troubles you
senses.definitionCN: 突然出现在脑海里、尤其令人不安的鲜活画面
senses.example: He could not erase the vision of the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 他无法抹去那栋空房子的影像。
senses.why: Memory replays an inner picture uninvited; seeing again without the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 记忆不请自来地重播内心画面，不用眼睛却像再次看见。

intro.en: Vision descends from Latin videre, to see, through the noun visio, the act or fact of seeing.
intro.cn: vision 源自拉丁语 videre（看），经名词 visio（看见的行为或事实）传入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *weid- means to see or to know, giving both sight and knowledge words across many languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 *weid- 意为看或知晓，在许多语言中同时衍生出「视」与「知」两族词。

items.en: Videre means to see; the derived noun visio means the act of seeing or a thing seen.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为看；派生名词 visio 意为看见的行为或所见之物。

items.en: The word enters French as vision, keeping both the physical and the imagined senses.
items.cn: 该词以 vision 进入法语，同时保留字面所见与想象所见两义。

items.en: English borrows vision in religious contexts first, meaning something seen in a dream or revelation.
items.cn: 英语最初在宗教语境借用 vision，指梦中或启示中所见的景象。

items.en: The ordinary sense of eyesight becomes established in English medical and everyday writing.
items.cn: 15 世纪，「视力」这一日常义在医学与日常文本中确立。

items.en: Vision now spans eyesight, imagination, and leadership, from blurry vision to a corporate vision statement.
items.cn: 如今 vision 涵盖视力、想象与领导远见，从视力模糊到企业愿景皆用此词。

note.en: Vision sits beside sight, sight-words, and dream-words; look-alikes share the Latin root, near meanings share the field of seeing and imagining.
note.cn: vision 与 sight、同根 see 族词、梦幻词相邻：形近组共享拉丁词根，近义组共享「看与想象」义场。

entries.definition: relating to seeing or the eyes
entries.definitionCN: 视觉的、用眼睛的；与 vision 同根的形容词

entries.definition: having or showing clear ideas about the future; a person with such ideas
entries.definitionCN: 有远见的（人）；由 vision 派生的形容词与名词

entries.definition: the act of dividing or the result of dividing
entries.definitionCN: 分开、分割；与 vision 拼写相近且同为 -sion 结尾，但词根不同，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a form or variant of something
entries.definitionCN: 版本、变体；同以 -sion 结尾，词根是 vertere（转），与 vision 词源不同

entries.definition: a face or appearance, especially in literary use
entries.definitionCN: 面容、外观；同出拉丁 videre 词族，属文学用词

entries.definition: the ability to see, or something that is seen
entries.definitionCN: 视力、景象；日耳曼词源的近义词，偏日常

entries.definition: the ability of the eyes to see
entries.definitionCN: 视力；只指生理能力，不含远义

entries.definition: a false idea or image that seems real
entries.definitionCN: 错觉、幻象；与幻象义相邻，但强调「假」

entries.definition: a series of images in sleep, or a strong hope
entries.definitionCN: 梦、梦想；与想象义相邻，偏愿望

entries.definition: the ability to see what will happen and prepare for it
entries.definitionCN: 预见、深谋远虑；与远见义相邻，强调提前防备

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin root videre, to see, and its real word family.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁词根 videre（看）及其真实词族。

normal.en: videre means to see; vision is literally the act of seeing.
normal.cn: videre 意为看；vision 字面就是「看的行为」。

normal.en: television lets you see across distance: tele- plus the same root.
normal.cn: television 让你看到远处：tele-（远）加同一词根。

normal.en: visual describes anything seen with the eyes.
normal.cn: visual 描述一切用眼睛看到的东西。

normal.en: envision is to see a plan inside your head before building it.
normal.cn: envision 是在动工之前先在脑中「看见」方案。

normal.en: visionary names a person who sees what others cannot yet see.
normal.cn: visionary 指能看见别人尚看不见之事的人。

abstract.en: Picture two lights in one eye: one for what is here, one for what could be.
abstract.cn: 想象眼睛里有两盏灯：一盏照亮眼前，一盏照向可能。

abstract.en: A fog lifts and the road ahead appears: that clearing is vision at work.
abstract.cn: 雾散路现：那片豁然开朗，正是 vision 在工作。

abstract.en: The mind's eye opens in the dark and draws a city that does not exist yet.
abstract.cn: 心灵的眼睛在黑暗中睁开，画出一座尚不存在的城。

examples.en: Years of night shifts slowly damaged his vision.
examples.cn: 多年的夜班慢慢损害了他的视力。

examples.en: The founder's vision was a library open to everyone in the city.
examples.cn: 创始人的构想是一座对全城开放的图书馆。

examples.en: A tall figure appeared at the edge of her vision and then was gone.
examples.cn: 一个高大的身影出现在她视野边缘，随即消失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「未整」——视力未整理好就看不清；远见是把未来的图景先「未雨绸缪地整」出来。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 videre（看）。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）+ 名词后缀构成 visio（看见的行为），经古法语 vision 进入英语。词根 *weid- 重构形式，同时衍生出 wit（智力）、view、evident 等词；「视」与「知」同源。

sensesIntro.en: From the eyes' power outward: sight, what is seen, the range of seeing, and finally the mind's eye that pictures the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 从眼睛的能力向外铺开：视力、所见之物、看的范围，最后到心灵的眼睛对未来构图的远见。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one act of seeing, from the eye outward to the mind
core.cn: 核心意象：同一次「看」，从眼睛延伸到心灵

branches.en: The physical act and its raw result
branches.cn: 生理之看及其直接产物：视力与景象

branches.en: Sight with boundaries: the field you can cover
branches.cn: 有边界的看：目光覆盖的视野

branches.en: Seeing without eyes: imagined, dreamed, or haunting pictures
branches.cn: 不用眼睛的看：想象、梦境与萦绕的画面

branches.en: Seeing turned wise: foresight and clear judgment
branches.cn: 看升华为智：远见与洞察

branches.en: Foresight fixed into a plan becomes a guiding purpose
branches.cn: 远见落成蓝图，便成为引领方向的目标

intro.en: The family of Latin videre spreads through prefixes that move the act of seeing toward, back, apart, or out.
intro.cn: videre 词族借助前缀把「看」引向不同方向：向前、向后、分开、向外。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, videre and its prefixed verbs built a dense family of seeing-words.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，videre 及其前缀动词构成了密集的「看」义词族。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 寡妇，字面为「被留下独自看顾的人」

derivatives.zh: 视觉的，由同根形容词构成
有远见的，由 vision 加后缀构成
设想，由 en- 加 vision 构成

definition_zh: 拜访、访问；参观、浏览（网站）；巡视、视察；作客、短暂逗留
definition_en: to go to see a person or place for a time, or to go to a website; to stay somewhere briefly
core_image: 一次登门：人走到另一个人或另一个地方面前，短暂停留再离开
scene: 门铃响起，门缝里已能看见客人的行李箱。They visit their grandmother every spring.
sceneCN: 这里 visit 是「探望、拜访」（第 1 个义项：专程去看某人）；句意为他们每年春天去看望祖母。走到人前、坐下说话，就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 动词：拜访；参观；视察；作客
名词：拜访；参观；访问

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「访客、参观者」，由动词加 -or 构成
名词，义为「正式访问、视察」，较少使用
形容词，义为「来访的」，如 visiting professor

senses.title: To go to see a person
senses.titleCN: 拜访：专程去看某人
senses.definition: to go to spend time with a person, especially socially or to show care
senses.definitionCN: 专程去与某人相处，尤其出于社交或关心
senses.example: They visit their grandmother every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们每年春天去看望祖母。
senses.why: Latin visere means to go to look at; seeing a person requires going to them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 visere 意为去看；要看人就得走到人面前。

senses.title: To go to a place
senses.titleCN: 参观：到某处走走看看
senses.definition: to go to a place to look at it or experience it
senses.definitionCN: 到某地去观看或体验
senses.example: Millions of people visit the old town each year.
senses.exampleCN: 每年有数百万人参观这座古镇。
senses.why: The looking widens from persons to places; the eye is the guest.
senses.whyCN: 「看」的对象从人扩展到地方，眼睛成了客人。

senses.title: To open a website
senses.titleCN: 浏览：访问网页或站点
senses.definition: to open and look at a website or an online page
senses.definitionCN: 打开并查看某个网站或网页
senses.example: The site gained ten thousand new visits this week.
senses.exampleCN: 该网站本周新增了一万次访问。
senses.why: Going somewhere becomes going to an address; the trip shrinks to a click.
senses.whyCN: 「去某地」变成「去某个地址」，行程缩短为一次点击。

senses.title: To inspect officially
senses.titleCN: 视察：以职务身份查看
senses.definition: to go to a place in an official role to check or examine it
senses.definitionCN: 以官方或职务身份前往查看、检查
senses.example: The minister visited the flood zone on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 部长周一视察了洪灾区。
senses.why: Looking becomes duty; the visit carries authority, not just curiosity.
senses.whyCN: 「看」变成职责，登门带着权威而非单纯好奇。

senses.title: To stay briefly
senses.titleCN: 作客：短暂逗留
senses.definition: to stay somewhere for a short time before leaving
senses.definitionCN: 在某处短暂停留后离开
senses.example: She visited the coast for two quiet weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 她在海边安静地小住了两周。
senses.why: Between arrival and departure lies the visit; time, not distance, defines it.
senses.whyCN: 到达与离开之间即是「访问」，界定它的是时长而非距离。

senses.title: To chat casually
senses.titleCN: 闲聊：坐下说说话
senses.definition: to talk with someone in a relaxed, friendly way, chiefly in American English
senses.definitionCN: 与某人轻松地聊天，主要用于美式英语
senses.example: The neighbors visited on the porch until dark.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们在门廊上聊天到天黑。
senses.why: A visit is for company more than for sight; the talk is the point.
senses.whyCN: 登门重在人伴而非看景，交谈本身成了目的。

senses.title: To come upon unwelcome
senses.titleCN: 降临：不快之事落到头上
senses.definition: of something unpleasant, to affect someone or something, formal or literary
senses.definitionCN: 指不好的事物降临或波及某人某地，正式或书面用法
senses.example: The storm visited the island without warning.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴毫无预兆地降临到那座岛上。
senses.why: The guest may bring trouble; an arrival is an arrival, welcome or not.
senses.whyCN: 客人也可能带来灾祸：到来就是到来，无论受欢迎与否。

senses.title: The act of visiting
senses.titleCN: 访问：作名词的一次登门
senses.definition: an occasion of going to see a person, place, or website
senses.definitionCN: 前往看望或查看某人、某地、某网页的一次行为
senses.example: The doctor's visit took less than an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 医生的出诊不到一小时就结束了。
senses.why: The whole journey gets a name; the act itself becomes a countable event.
senses.whyCN: 整趟行程获得名字，「去一趟」本身成了可数的名词。

intro.en: Visit comes from Latin visere, to go to look at, a frequentative form of videre, to see, through Old French visiter.
intro.cn: visit 源自拉丁语 visere（去看），是 videre（看）的反复态形式，经古法语 visiter 进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *weid- means to see or to know, the same root behind vision and wise.
items.cn: 重构词根 *weid- 意为看或知晓，与 vision、wise 同根。

items.en: Visere, to go to see, forms the noun visitare, to pay repeated visits.
items.cn: 拉丁语 visere 意为去看；派生 visitare 意为屡次造访。

items.en: In Late Latin visitare takes on religious use: a bishop's pastoral visits to his flock.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中 visitare 兼有宗教用法：主教巡视信众。

items.en: The word passes into French as visiter, keeping both social and official senses.
items.cn: 该词以 visiter 进入法语，同时保留社交与公务两义。

items.en: English borrows visit first in religious and official contexts, meaning to comfort or inspect.
items.cn: 英语最初在宗教与公务语境借用 visit，意为安抚或巡视。

items.en: The everyday senses of calling on people, touring places, and browsing websites all grow from that one trip to look.
items.cn: 日常的探望、游览与浏览网页，都由那一次「走去看」生长而来。

note.en: Look-alikes share the see-root or the spelling; near meanings share the field of going and calling on.
note.cn: 形近组共享「看」词根或拼写，近义组共享「前往、造访」义场。

entries.definition: a person who visits
entries.definitionCN: 访客、参观者；由 visit 加 -or 构成

entries.definition: the ability to see, or an imagined picture
entries.definitionCN: 视力、想象；同出 *weid- 词根，仅词根相同、语义分工不同

entries.definition: a movable part of a helmet that protects the face
entries.definitionCN: 头盔面甲；拼写相近但词源为法兰西语系的护面部件，与 visit 词源不同

entries.definition: a long view through an opening
entries.definitionCN: 远眺的景致；同为「看」族但来自意大利语，词根借自拉丁 videre，属旁支词族

entries.definition: a tool that grips things firmly
entries.definitionCN: 台钳；美式拼写，与 visit 只是字母相近，词源为拉丁 vitis（葡萄藤），不同源

entries.definition: to visit someone briefly, often formally
entries.definitionCN: 短暂拜访某人，常带正式色彩

entries.definition: to visit several places as part of a journey
entries.definitionCN: 巡游、观光；强调多站行程，visit 强调单次登门

entries.definition: to go often to a place
entries.definitionCN: 常去某处；强调反复，visit 无此义

entries.definition: to examine something officially and carefully
entries.definitionCN: 检查、视察；与视察义相邻，但看得更细

entries.definition: to remain somewhere for a time
entries.definitionCN: 停留、暂住；与作客义相邻，但不必然包含「走去看人」

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin root visere, to go and look.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁词根 visere（走去看）。

normal.en: visere means to go to look; a visit is a trip made for seeing.
normal.cn: visere 意为走去看；visit 就是为「看」而走的一趟。

normal.en: visitor is the person on the trip; visit is the trip itself.
normal.cn: visitor 是赶路看人的人，visit 是这趟行程本身。

normal.en: television and visit share the same old see-root.
normal.cn: television 与 visit 共享同一个古老的「看」词根。

normal.en: supervise is to watch from above; the same root watches in both words.
normal.cn: supervise 是从上往下看；两个词里都是同一词根在看。

normal.en: visiting hours name the time when guests may come to look and stay.
normal.cn: visiting hours 是客人可以来看望并停留的时段。

abstract.en: A suitcase by the door: the trip to see someone begins before the door opens.
abstract.cn: 门边的行李箱：见人的行程在开门之前就开始了。

abstract.en: One chair pulled closer to the table: someone has come to sit for a while.
abstract.cn: 椅子被拉近桌边：有人来了，要坐一会儿。

abstract.en: A short visit leaves a long shadow: you go, but the warmth stays.
abstract.cn: 短暂的拜访留下长长的余温：人走了，暖意还在。

examples.en: We visit the museum whenever a new exhibition opens.
examples.cn: 每逢新展开幕，我们都会去参观博物馆。

examples.en: Please visit our website for the full schedule.
examples.cn: 完整日程请浏览我们的网站。

examples.en: The bishop's visit to the village was recorded in the parish book.
examples.cn: 主教对村庄的巡视被记录在教区簿册里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「未见得」——不去看就未见得知道朋友近况；visit 的字面正是「走去看」。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 visere（走去看）。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）的反复态 visere（走去看）→ visitare（屡次造访）→ 古法语 visiter → 英语 visit。与 vision、view、wit 同出印欧词根 *weid-（重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: One trip to look branches by destination: a person, a place, a page, or an official duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一次「走去看」，按目的地分化：看人、看地、看网页、看公务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one trip made in order to see
core.cn: 核心意象：为了看而走的一趟

branches.en: Seeing people: the call and the company it brings
branches.cn: 看人：登门拜访与随之而来的陪伴

branches.en: Seeing places: touring and the short stay after arriving
branches.cn: 看地：参观与到达后的短暂停留

branches.en: The trip shrinks to a click on a page
branches.cn: 行程缩成一次点击，看的是网页

branches.en: The look carries duty: official inspection
branches.cn: 看带上职责：公务视察

branches.en: The arrival itself, welcome or not, becomes the named event
branches.cn: 到来本身，无论好坏，成为被命名的一次访问

intro.en: The visit-family keeps the see-root behind prefixes that direct the looking.
intro.cn: visit 词族用前缀引导同一个「看」词根的方向。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre built prefixed verbs for every direction of seeing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 为「看」的各个方向都造了前缀动词。

derivatives.zh: 访客，由 visit 加 -or 构成
正式访问，由 visit 加 -ion 构成

definition_zh: 访客、来访者；参观者；候鸟、季节性来客
definition_en: a person who visits a place or person, or a bird or animal that appears in an area for a season
core_image: 门口按下门铃的人：带着来意，短暂停留
scene: 前台登记簿翻开在最新一页，笔还未放下。Every visitor must sign in at the desk.
sceneCN: 这里 visitor 是「访客、来访者」（第 1 个义项：到访某地的人）；句意为每位访客必须在前台登记。敲门的那个人，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 名词：访客；参观者；候鸟

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「拜访、参观」，是本词的动词基础
名词，义为「正式访问、视察」

senses.title: A person who comes to see someone
senses.titleCN: 访客：登门看望他人的人
senses.definition: a person who goes to see another person, especially socially or at home
senses.definitionCN: 去见另一个人的人，尤其出于社交目的或到家中
senses.example: Every visitor must sign in at the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 每位访客必须在前台登记。
senses.why: The agent suffix -or turns the act of visiting into the one who does it.
senses.whyCN: 施动后缀 -or 把「拜访」这一行为变成做这件事的人。

senses.title: A person who comes to a place
senses.titleCN: 参观者：到某处游览或办事的人
senses.definition: a person who goes to a place such as a museum, park, or office
senses.definitionCN: 前往博物馆、公园或办公室等场所的人
senses.example: The museum greets two thousand visitors on a free day.
senses.exampleCN: 免费开放日，博物馆迎接两千名参观者。
senses.why: The destination widens from a person to any door worth entering.
senses.whyCN: 目的地从一个人扩展到任何值得进入的门。

senses.title: A temporary member
senses.titleCN: 外来者：临时加入的成员或选手
senses.definition: a person away from their usual team, school, or club, especially a visiting player
senses.definitionCN: 临时到访别队、别校或俱乐部的成员，尤指客队选手
senses.example: The visitors opened the match with a goal in the first minute.
senses.exampleCN: 客队在开场第一分钟就攻入一球。
senses.why: A guest on another's ground is still a visitor, even in a match.
senses.whyCN: 在别人场地上作客的人仍是访客，赛场上亦然。

senses.title: A seasonal guest in nature
senses.titleCN: 候鸟：季节性出现的鸟兽
senses.definition: a bird or animal that appears in an area only at certain times of the year
senses.definitionCN: 一年中只在特定时节出现在某地的鸟类或动物
senses.example: Winter visitors return to the wetland every November.
senses.exampleCN: 冬候鸟每年十一月回到这片湿地。
senses.why: Nature also arrives and departs; the season plays the host.
senses.whyCN: 自然界同样有来有往，季节扮演了主人。

intro.en: Visitor is visit plus the Latin agent suffix -or: simply the one who visits.
intro.cn: visitor 由 visit 加拉丁施动后缀 -or 构成：字面即「去拜访的人」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *weid- means to see or to know, shared with vision and wise.
items.cn: 重构词根 *weid- 意为看或知晓，与 vision、wise 同根。

items.en: Visere means to go and look; visitare means to visit repeatedly.
items.cn: 拉丁语 visere 意为走去看；visitare 意为屡次造访。

items.en: The agent noun visitator names the official who inspects, especially a church visitor.
items.cn: 施动名词 visitator 指执行巡视的官员，尤指教会的巡访者。

items.en: The word travels through French forms related to visiter.
items.cn: 该词经法语 visiter 一族传入英语。

items.en: Visitor appears in English in both official and social uses, and later covers tourists and guests at large.
items.cn: visitor 在英语中先用于公务与社交场合，后泛指游客与来客。

note.en: Look-alikes keep the visit-root or the spelling; near meanings name other kinds of guests and arrivals.
note.cn: 形近组保留 visit 词根或拼写，近义组指称其他类型的来客。

entries.definition: to go to see a person or place; the act of visiting
entries.definitionCN: 拜访、参观；visitor 的动词与名词基础

entries.definition: the ability to see or an imagined picture
entries.definitionCN: 视力、想象；同出「看」词根，与 visitor 词根相同而语义不同

entries.definition: a movable face cover of a helmet
entries.definitionCN: 头盔面甲；与 visitor 拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the winner of a contest
entries.definitionCN: 胜者；词根为拉丁 vincere（战胜），与 visitor 词源不同，仅拼写相近

entries.definition: a person who watches over an examination
entries.definitionCN: 监考人；同为巡视性质的人物，但词根是拉丁 vigilare（守望），不同源

entries.definition: a person invited to someone's home or event
entries.definitionCN: 宾客；强调受邀，visitor 不必然受邀请

entries.definition: a person traveling for pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 游客；只为游乐，visitor 目的更宽

entries.definition: a person who makes a short visit, chiefly British
entries.definitionCN: 短暂来访的人，主要用于英式英语

entries.definition: a person who has just come
entries.definitionCN: 刚到达的人；强调到达动作，visitor 强调探访身份

entries.definition: a bird or animal that moves seasonally
entries.definitionCN: 迁徙的鸟兽；与候鸟义相邻，强调移动过程

normalIntro.en: Five anchors built on visit plus the agent suffix -or.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，建立在 visit 加施动后缀 -or 之上。

normal.en: visit is the act; visitor is the one who acts.
normal.cn: visit 是行为，visitor 是做这个行为的人。

normal.en: -or marks the doer, as in actor and inventor.
normal.cn: -or 标记做事的人，如 actor、inventor。

normal.en: visitor center is the first stop for arrivals in a park.
normal.cn: 游客中心是来客在公园的第一站。

normal.en: the visiting team is called the visitors in sports.
normal.cn: 体育比赛里客队就叫 the visitors。

normal.en: winter visitors in birdwatching mean birds that come for the season.
normal.cn: 观鸟人说的 winter visitors 指按季节到来的鸟类。

abstract.en: A doorbell in winter dusk: someone stands outside with a reason to come in.
abstract.cn: 冬日黄昏的门铃：门外站着一个人，带着走进来的理由。

abstract.en: The guest book fills with names, each one a short story of arrival.
abstract.cn: 访客簿写满名字，每个名字都是一段抵达的小故事。

abstract.en: Birds crossing the sky in November are visitors the season sends.
abstract.cn: 十一月掠过天空的鸟，是季节派来的访客。

examples.en: The gallery counts its visitors with a sensor at the door.
examples.cn: 美术馆用门口的传感器统计参观人数。

examples.en: An unexpected visitor arrived while we were having dinner.
examples.cn: 我们正吃晚饭时来了一位不速之客。

examples.en: Summer visitors bring the small town its busiest months.
examples.cn: 夏季来客给小镇带来一年最繁忙的几个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「慰自特」——来访的客人自带慰藉，特意来看你。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 visitare（屡次造访）加施动后缀 -or。

root: 拉丁语 visitare（屡次造访）+ 施动后缀 -or（……的人）→ 英语 visitor，即「去拜访的人」。词根 videre（看）与 vision、view 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One suffix, one doer; the word widens from people who call on people to crowds, teams, and seasonal birds.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个后缀造出一个「人」：从登门的人扩展到游客、客队与候鸟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one who arrives to see
core.cn: 核心意象：为了看而到来的人

branches.en: The guest who comes to a person
branches.cn: 登门看人的人：访客

branches.en: The crowd that comes to a place
branches.cn: 到访场所的人群：参观者

branches.en: The team on another's ground
branches.cn: 站在别人场地上的一方：客队

branches.en: The bird the season sends
branches.cn: 季节派来的鸟：候鸟

branches.en: Every arrival signs the same book
branches.cn: 无论看人看地，每次到访都记在同一本簿子上

intro.en: The word is a small machine: root of seeing plus an agent suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词像一台小机器：看的词根加上施动后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin loved agent suffixes; -or is the classic doer-ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语偏爱施动后缀；-or 是经典的「做事者」词尾。

derivatives.zh: 拜访，visitor 的动词基础
正式访问，由 visit 加 -ion 构成

definition_zh: 视觉的、看得见的；直观展示的图像
definition_en: relating to seeing or the eyes; a picture or display used to show something
core_image: 投影仪亮起：白墙上出现所有人都看得见的画面
scene: 会议室灯光暗下，白墙亮起第一张图表。The report uses strong visuals to explain the data.
sceneCN: 这里 visual 是「视觉展示物」（第 3 个义项：用来说明的图像）；句意为报告用醒目的图像来解释数据。灯光下人人都看得见的画面，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 形容词：视觉的；看得见的
名词：视觉资料、图像展示

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「在视觉上」，由形容词加 -ly 构成
名词，义为「视力、想象」，同根名词
动词，义为「使形象化、想象」，由 visual 加 -ize 构成
形容词，义为「视听的」，由 audio- 加 visual 构成

senses.title: Of the eyes
senses.titleCN: 视觉的：与看和眼睛相关
senses.definition: connected with seeing or with the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 与观看或眼睛有关
senses.example: Reading is a visual skill learned step by step.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读是一种逐步习得的视觉技能。
senses.why: The adjective pins the whole act of seeing onto the noun it modifies.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把「看」这一行为整体固定到所修饰的名词上。

senses.title: Able to be seen
senses.titleCN: 看得见的：肉眼可察觉
senses.definition: visible or able to be noticed by the eye
senses.definitionCN: 可见的、能被眼睛察觉的
senses.example: The crack shows a visual sign of the building's age.
senses.exampleCN: 裂缝是这座建筑年代的肉眼可见的迹象。
senses.why: What exists for the eye exists plainly; sight is the proof.
senses.whyCN: 对眼睛而言存在的东西确凿可见，看见即证明。

senses.title: A picture used to show
senses.titleCN: 图像：用来说明的视觉展示物
senses.definition: a picture, chart, or display used to explain or present something
senses.definitionCN: 用于解释或展示的图画、图表或演示
senses.example: The report uses strong visuals to explain the data.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用醒目的图像来解释数据。
senses.why: The adjective steps forward as a noun: the thing meant for the eye.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作名词：专供眼睛看的东西。

senses.title: Of optical devices
senses.titleCN: 光学装置的：帮助看的仪器
senses.definition: of instruments that help or extend the eye, such as lenses
senses.definitionCN: 属于帮助或延伸眼睛的仪器，如镜片
senses.example: The patient chose new visual aids last week.
senses.exampleCN: 病人上周选配了新的助视器。
senses.why: The eye gains tools; the word labels anything that serves sight.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛有了工具，这个词标示一切服务于视觉的器械。

intro.en: Visual is the adjective of the Latin see-root videre, built with the suffix -ual.
intro.cn: visual 是拉丁「看」词根 videre 的形容词形式，由后缀 -ual 构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *weid- means to see or to know.
items.cn: 重构词根 *weid- 意为看或知晓。

items.en: Videre means to see; the adjective visualis means of sight or seeing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为看；形容词 visualis 意为视觉的。

items.en: Visualis appears in late philosophical Latin, distinguishing knowledge from sight.
items.cn: visualis 出现在晚期哲学拉丁语中，用以区分认知与视觉。

items.en: English borrows visual as a term of optics and anatomy before it becomes everyday.
items.cn: 英语先在光学与解剖学语境借用 visual，后转为日常用词。

items.en: The noun use for pictures in media and talks is a twentieth-century development.
items.cn: 指代媒体与演讲中图片的名词用法是二十世纪的发展。

note.en: Look-alikes share the see-root; near meanings cover the visible world and its pictures.
note.cn: 形近组共享「看」词根，近义组涵盖可见世界及其图像。

entries.definition: the ability to see or an imagined picture
entries.definitionCN: 视力、想象；visual 的同根名词

entries.definition: to form a picture in the mind
entries.definitionCN: 使形象化、想象；visual 加 -ize 构成

entries.definition: relaxed and informal
entries.definitionCN: 随意的；与 visual 拼写尾段相近，词根为拉丁 casus（偶然），不同源

entries.definition: happening in the ordinary way
entries.definitionCN: 通常的；词根为拉丁 usus（使用），与 visual 词源不同，仅拼写相近

entries.definition: a face or appearance
entries.definitionCN: 面容；同出「看」词族的文学用词

entries.definition: able to be seen
entries.definitionCN: 可见的；与看得见义相邻，visible 强调状态，visual 强调领域

entries.definition: relating to light and vision, especially instruments
entries.definitionCN: 光学的；与光学装置义相邻

entries.definition: of drawing or pictures that show information
entries.definitionCN: 图示的；与图像义相邻，偏绘制

entries.definition: shown in pictures
entries.definitionCN: 图片的；与图像义相邻，偏叙事图画

entries.definition: of the eye itself, formal or medical
entries.definitionCN: 眼睛的，正式或医学用语

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the adjective of the see-root.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自「看」词根的形容词。

normal.en: visual is what belongs to the eyes.
normal.cn: visual 属于眼睛。

normal.en: audiovisual pairs sound with sight in one word.
normal.cn: audiovisual 把声音与视觉放进一个词。

normal.en: visual arts are the arts you look at, like painting and film.
normal.cn: 视觉艺术是供观看的艺术，如绘画与电影。

normal.en: visualize means to make an inner picture, adding -ize to visual.
normal.cn: visualize 是在脑中成像，由 visual 加 -ize 构成。

normal.en: visually compares with verbally: by eye versus by word.
normal.cn: visually 与 verbally 相对：靠眼看与靠话讲。

abstract.en: A beam of light from a projector: everything it touches becomes visual.
abstract.cn: 投影仪的一束光：它照到哪里，哪里就变成视觉的。

abstract.en: Eyes open, the world arrives; eyes closed, only the inner picture remains.
abstract.cn: 睁眼世界到来，闭眼只剩内心的画面。

abstract.en: A chart on white paper: numbers turned into something the eye can grasp.
abstract.cn: 白纸上的图表：数字变成了眼睛能抓住的东西。

examples.en: The teacher added a visual to every hard concept.
examples.cn: 老师为每个难点概念都配了一幅图示。

examples.en: Noise pollution is invisible, but light pollution has clear visual effects.
examples.cn: 噪声污染不可见，而光污染有清晰的视觉影响。

examples.en: The film relies on visual storytelling rather than dialogue.
examples.cn: 这部电影依靠视觉叙事而非对白。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂小姐」——喂给眼睛看的小姐就是「视觉的」画面；谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 visualis（视觉的）。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看）→ visualis（视觉的）→ 英语 visual。同根词 vision、view、evident；形容词后缀 -ual 表示「与……相关」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective of seeing spreads from the eyes to the visible, then to the pictures made for the eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 「看」的形容词从眼睛铺向可见之物，再到专供眼睛的图像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything that belongs to the eye
core.cn: 核心意象：一切属于眼睛的东西

branches.en: The eye and its skill, like reading
branches.cn: 眼睛及其技能，如阅读

branches.en: What the eye can catch in the world
branches.cn: 世界中眼睛能捕捉的：可见之物

branches.en: Pictures made for eyes, charts and screens
branches.cn: 专为眼睛制作的图像、图表与屏幕

branches.en: Tools that carry sight further, lenses and aids
branches.cn: 延伸视线的工具：镜片与助视器

branches.en: Shared displays let many eyes see one thing
branches.cn: 共享的展示让许多眼睛看同一件事

intro.en: The see-root wears suffixes and prefixes to become adjectives, verbs, and nouns.
intro.cn: 「看」词根加上各种前后缀，构成形容词、动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin visualis already had the modern shape of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 visualis 已具备这个词的现代形态。

derivatives.zh: 在视觉上，由 visual 加 -ly 构成
使形象化，由 visual 加 -ize 构成
视听的，由 audio- 加 visual 构成

definition_zh: 极其重要的、必不可少的；维持生命所必需的；有活力的、生机勃勃的
definition_en: extremely important and necessary; connected with or needed for life; full of energy
core_image: 跳动的脉搏：少了它生命就停下来的那一件事
scene: 手术室的仪器发出规律的滴声，监护屏上的波线从未中断。Clean water is vital for the patients' recovery.
sceneCN: 这里 vital 是「必不可少的」（第 2 个义项：对生命或结果不可或缺）；句意为清洁用水对病人的康复至关重要。像脉搏一样不能停，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 形容词：极其重要的；维持生命所必需的；有活力的

collocations.zh: 一座生机勃勃、不断发展的城市

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「活力、生命力」，由 vital 加 -ity 构成
副词，义为「极其、紧要地」
动词，义为「使充满活力」，较少使用
动词，义为「使恢复生机」，由 re- 加 vitalize 构成
名词，义为「维生素」，与 vital 同源词族

senses.title: Necessary for life
senses.titleCN: 维持生命所必需的
senses.definition: needed by a living body to stay alive
senses.definitionCN: 生物体存活所必需的
senses.example: The monitors tracked each patient's vital signs.
senses.exampleCN: 监护仪追踪每位病人的生命体征。
senses.why: Latin vita means life; anything tied to life itself is vital.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vita 意为生命；与生命本身相连的即是 vital。

senses.title: Extremely important
senses.titleCN: 极其重要的：不可或缺
senses.definition: so important that something fails without it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到缺少它事情就无法进行的
senses.example: Clean water is vital for the patients' recovery.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁用水对病人的康复至关重要。
senses.why: What the body cannot live without, a plan cannot succeed without: life's logic applied to work.
senses.whyCN: 身体离之不能活的东西，计划离之不能成：生命的逻辑用到事务上。

senses.title: Full of energy
senses.titleCN: 有活力的：充满生机
senses.definition: lively, energetic, and full of strength
senses.definitionCN: 有生气、精力充沛、充满力量的
senses.example: She remained vital well into her nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 她年逾九十仍然活力不减。
senses.why: Where life concentrates, energy shows; the word brightens with living force.
senses.whyCN: 生命力聚集之处便显出能量，这个词随之带上生气的光亮。

senses.title: Deathly or life-related in old use
senses.titleCN: 生死攸关的：旧式用法
senses.definition: relating to life and death, in older or formal use
senses.definitionCN: 涉及生死，见于旧式或正式用法
senses.example: The wound struck a vital part.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口击中了要害部位。
senses.why: The parts that hold life are the parts whose loss ends it.
senses.whyCN: 维系生命的部位，一旦失去便终结生命，故称要害。

intro.en: Vital is Latin vita, life, turned into an adjective: everything that belongs to life.
intro.cn: vital 由拉丁语 vita（生命）变成的形容词：一切属于生命的东西。

items.en: The reconstructed root *gweih- means to live, behind both Latin vivere and vita.
items.cn: 重构词根 *gweih- 意为活，是拉丁 vivere 与 vita 的共同来源。

items.en: Vita means life; vitalis means of life, life-giving, or necessary to life.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vita 意为生命；vitalis 意为属于生命的、给予生命的。

items.en: The word passes through French vital with the same senses.
items.cn: 该词经法语 vital 传入，义项基本不变。

items.en: English takes vital in medical and theological texts, meaning of life or essential to it.
items.cn: 英语在医学与神学文本中先取 vital，意为生命的或生命必需的。

items.en: The everyday sense of extremely important grows from the medical one, and the energetic sense keeps the Latin fire.
items.cn: 「极其重要」的日常义由医学义生长而来，而「有活力」义保留了拉丁语的生命之火。

note.en: Look-alikes share the life-root or the spelling; near meanings range from essential to lively.
note.cn: 形近组共享「生命」词根或拼写，近义组从「不可或缺」延伸到「活泼」。

entries.definition: energy and liveliness
entries.definitionCN: 活力、生命力；vital 加 -ity 构成

entries.definition: a substance needed for health, coined as the amine of life
entries.definitionCN: 维生素；造词时取「生命之胺」之意，同 vita 词根

entries.definition: the organs necessary for life
entries.definitionCN: 生命器官（心、肺等）；vital 的复数名词用法

entries.definition: a small bottle for medicine
entries.definitionCN: 小药瓶；与 vital 拼写相近但词源为拉丁 phialis（玻璃瓶），不同源

entries.definition: food or provisions, old use
entries.definitionCN: 食物、给养（旧用法）；发音与 vital 相近，词根为拉丁 victualia（给养），词源不同

entries.definition: absolutely necessary
entries.definitionCN: 必需的；与极其重要义相邻，essential 强调本质，vital 强调性命攸关

entries.definition: deciding success or failure
entries.definitionCN: 决定成败的；强调关键节点

entries.definition: impossible to do without
entries.definitionCN: 不可或缺的；语气更绝对

entries.definition: of decisive importance or at a turning point
entries.definitionCN: 关键的、危急的；兼有临界义

entries.definition: full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛的；与有活力义相邻，不含生命必需义

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from Latin vita, life.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 vita（生命）。

normal.en: vita means life; vital means belonging to life.
normal.cn: vita 意为生命；vital 即属于生命的。

normal.en: vital signs are the readings that show a body is alive.
normal.cn: vital signs 是显示身体存活的生命体征。

normal.en: vitamin was coined as the amine of life.
normal.cn: vitamin 造词时意为「生命之胺」。

normal.en: revitalize is to give life back, re- plus vitalize.
normal.cn: revitalize 是重新赋予生机，re- 加 vitalize。

normal.en: a vital organ is one the body cannot lose and live.
normal.cn: vital organ 是身体失去即无法存活的器官。

abstract.en: A pulse on a screen: the line that must never go flat.
abstract.cn: 屏幕上的脉搏：那条绝不能变平的线。

abstract.en: Air in a sealed room: invisible, unnoticed, and suddenly everything.
abstract.cn: 密室中的空气：平时无感，缺时便是一切。

abstract.en: A city at rush hour that still hums after midnight: its vital energy.
abstract.cn: 午夜过后仍然嗡嗡作响的城市：它的活力。

examples.en: Trust is vital to any team that shares one goal.
examples.cn: 信任对任何共赴一目标的团队都至关重要。

examples.en: The nurse checked the patient's vital signs every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时检查一次病人的生命体征。

examples.en: Even a small garden can look vital in spring.
examples.cn: 哪怕小花园，春天也能显得生机勃勃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪透」——身体歪透了就没了生命体征；凡是 vital 的东西，歪一点都不行。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 vita（生命）。

root: 拉丁语 vita（生命）+ 形容词后缀 -alis → vitalis → 法语 vital → 英语 vital。印欧词根 *gweih-（重构形式）同时衍生 vivere（活）、vitamin、revive 等词。

sensesIntro.en: Life first, then everything life depends on, then the brightness of living itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是生命本身，继而是一切生命所依赖之物，最后是生命本身的光亮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life itself as the measure of importance
core.cn: 核心意象：以生命本身为重要性的标尺

branches.en: Life in the body: signs, organs, and the parts that hold life
branches.cn: 身体里的生命：体征、器官与维系生命的要害

branches.en: Life's logic borrowed by plans and projects
branches.cn: 计划的逻辑借用生命的逻辑：不可或缺

branches.en: Life showing as energy in a person or city
branches.cn: 生命以能量显现于人或城市

branches.en: What ends things when lost is vital, in body or in plan
branches.cn: 无论身体还是计划，失去即终结者即为 vital

branches.en: From bare survival to flourishing vitality
branches.cn: 从勉强存活到蓬勃生机

intro.en: The life-root spreads through prefixes and suffixes into a family of living words.
intro.cn: 「生命」词根借助前后缀铺成一个「生」义词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vivere, to live, and vita, life, built the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vivere（活）与 vita（生命）构建了整个词族。

derivatives.zh: 活力，由 vital 加 -ity 构成
极其，由 vital 加 -ly 构成
使恢复生机，由 re- 加 vitalize 构成

definition_zh: 嗓音、说话声；意见、发言权；语态；表达、说出
definition_en: the sound made when speaking or singing; the right to express an opinion; a verb form showing action; to express in words
core_image: 从喉咙到会场的通道：一个声音由内向外被听见
scene: 会议桌旁的手一只只举起，记录员抬起头。Members voiced their doubts about the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 voice 是动词「表达、说出」（第 4 个义项：把想法说出来）；句意为成员们对计划表达了自己的疑虑。声音从喉咙走到会场，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 名词：嗓音；意见；语态
动词：表达、说出

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「有声的、浊音的」，语音学术语
形容词，义为「无声的、清音的；没有发言权的」
形容词，义为「嗓音的；直言的」，同源词

senses.title: The sound of speaking
senses.titleCN: 嗓音：说话时发出的声音
senses.definition: the sound a person makes when speaking or singing
senses.definitionCN: 人说话或唱歌时发出的声音
senses.example: Her voice carried to the back of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音一直传到大厅后排。
senses.why: Latin vox names the sound of the throat; the word is that sound itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vox 命名喉咙发出的声响，这个词就是那声响。

senses.title: The right to speak
senses.titleCN: 发言权：表达意见的资格
senses.definition: the right or opportunity to express an opinion in decisions
senses.definitionCN: 在决策中表达意见的权利或机会
senses.example: Workers finally gained a voice in company policy.
senses.exampleCN: 员工终于在公司政策上有了发言权。
senses.why: A sound that counts in decisions becomes a right; being heard becomes having a say.
senses.whyCN: 在决策中有分量的声音变成一种权利：被听见即有话语权。

senses.title: Grammar's form
senses.titleCN: 语态：动词的主被动形式
senses.definition: the verb form showing whether the subject acts or is acted upon
senses.definitionCN: 表示主语发出动作还是承受动作的动词形式
senses.example: The teacher rewrote the sentence in the active voice.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把句子改写成主动语态。
senses.why: The verb answers who speaks and who is spoken of; grammar calls it voice.
senses.whyCN: 动词回答谁在说话、谁被说到，语法称之为语态。

senses.title: To express aloud
senses.titleCN: 表达：把想法说出
senses.definition: to state a feeling, fear, or opinion in words
senses.definitionCN: 用言语说出感受、担忧或看法
senses.example: Members voiced their doubts about the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 成员们对计划表达了自己的疑虑。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: to give what is inside a sound outside.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词：把心里的东西赋予外部的声音。

senses.title: Inner urge
senses.titleCN: 心声：内心的声音或召唤
senses.definition: an inner feeling or calling, often literary
senses.definitionCN: 内心的感受或召唤，多用于文学
senses.example: He followed the quiet voice of his conscience.
senses.exampleCN: 他听从了良心安静的声音。
senses.why: The throat's sound turns inward; conscience and desire learn to speak.
senses.whyCN: 喉咙的声音转向内心，良知与欲望学会了「说话」。

intro.en: Voice descends from Latin vox, vocis, the sound of a speaking throat, through Old French voiz.
intro.cn: voice 源自拉丁语 vox（呼格 vocis），即说话时喉咙发出的声音，经古法语 voiz 进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wekw- means to speak or to give voice, behind both vox and vocare.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wekw- 意为说话或发出声音，是 vox 与 vocare 的共同来源。

items.en: Vox means voice; the verb vocare means to call, both from the same root.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vox 意为声音；动词 vocare 意为呼唤，同出一词根。

items.en: The word becomes voiz in French, keeping the sound and the opinion senses.
items.cn: 该词在法语中作 voiz，同时保留声音与意见两义。

items.en: English borrows voice first for sound and expression, then for representation in councils.
items.cn: 英语先借 voice 指声音与表达，随后指议事中的代表发言权。

items.en: The grammatical sense of voice develops in European language studies.
items.cn: 16 世纪起，voice 的语法「语态」义在欧洲语言研究中确立。

items.en: The verb to voice and phrases like give voice to complete the journey from throat to opinion.
items.cn: 动词 voice 与短语 give voice to 完成了从喉咙到意见的全程。

note.en: Look-alikes share the call-root; near meanings gather the words of sound and saying.
note.cn: 形近组共享「呼唤」词根，近义组汇集声音与言说之词。

entries.definition: of the voice; willing to speak out
entries.definitionCN: 嗓音的；直言的；与 voice 同根的形容词

entries.definition: a strong call to a career or way of life
entries.definitionCN: 使命感、天职；同出 vocare（呼唤）词根

entries.definition: to speak in favor of; a person who does so
entries.definitionCN: 提倡、拥护者；ad-（向）加 vocare，为「把声音递过去」

entries.definition: immoral behavior or a tool for gripping
entries.definitionCN: 恶习、老虎钳；与 voice 拼写相近但词根为拉丁 vitium 或 vitis，不同源

entries.definition: the act of choosing
entries.definitionCN: 选择；与 voice 韵母相近，词源为拉丁 eligere，不同源

entries.definition: anything heard
entries.definitionCN: 声音；泛指一切声响，voice 专指人喉

entries.definition: a belief or judgment
entries.definitionCN: 意见；与发言权义相邻，voice 强调说出

entries.definition: a right to influence decisions, in phrases like have a say
entries.definitionCN: 话语权，用于 have a say 等短语

entries.definition: to show thoughts or feelings in words
entries.definitionCN: 表达；与动词义相邻，路径更宽

entries.definition: something spoken, formal
entries.definitionCN: 说出的话，正式用语

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from Latin vox and vocare, sound and call.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自拉丁语 vox（声音）与 vocare（呼唤）。

normal.en: vox means voice; the English word keeps the sound alive.
normal.cn: vox 意为声音；英语词保留了它的声响。

normal.en: vocal people use their voice willingly.
normal.cn: vocal 的人乐于发声。

normal.en: vocation is a calling, the same root calling you.
normal.cn: vocation 是召唤，同一词根在呼唤你。

normal.en: advocate is to call toward something, to speak for it.
normal.cn: advocate 是向某处呼唤，即为它发声。

normal.en: passive and active are the two voices of grammar.
normal.cn: 被动与主动是语法的两种语态。

abstract.en: One throat among many, and suddenly the room turns quiet to listen.
abstract.cn: 众人中一副喉咙开口，满屋忽然安静下来听。

abstract.en: A raised hand becomes a raised voice becomes a counted vote.
abstract.cn: 举起的手变成扬起的声，再变成被计入的一票。

abstract.en: Conscience knocks inside like a small door with its own voice.
abstract.cn: 良知在内心叩门，像一扇自带声音的小门。

examples.en: He lost his voice after the long lecture.
examples.cn: 长篇讲课之后他的嗓子哑了。

examples.en: The report gave voice to families who had never been asked.
examples.cn: 这份报告让从未被问过的家庭发出了声音。

examples.en: Several senators voiced concerns about the budget.
examples.cn: 几位参议员表达了对预算的担忧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我嘶」——喊到「我嘶」哑了嗓子；voice 就是「我」发出的声音。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 vox（声音）。

root: 拉丁语 vox（声音，词干 voc-）→ 古法语 voiz → 英语 voice。印欧词根 *wekw-（重构形式，说话）同时衍生 vocal、vocation、advocate、invoke 等。

sensesIntro.en: From the throat outward: the sound, the right to make it, grammar's turn-taking, and the verb that dares to speak.
sensesIntro.cn: 从喉咙向外：声音、发声的权利、语法里的角色分工，以及敢于开口的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sound traveling from inside to outside
core.cn: 核心意象：声音由内向外传播

branches.en: The physical sound of a throat
branches.cn: 喉咙发出的物理声响：嗓音

branches.en: The sound that counts: rights and stated opinions
branches.cn: 有分量的声音：发言权与说出的意见

branches.en: Who acts, who is acted on: grammar's voice
branches.cn: 谁行动、谁承受：语法中的语态

branches.en: The sound turns inward as conscience
branches.cn: 声音转向内心，成为良知的心声

branches.en: From outer sound to inner call, one channel
branches.cn: 从外部的声音到内心的召唤，同一条通道

intro.en: The call-root voc- carries speaking into every corner of the language.
intro.cn: 「呼唤」词根 voc- 把「说」带进语言的每个角落。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare, to call, and vox, voice, built a large family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare（呼唤）与 vox（声音）构建了庞大的词族。

derivatives.zh: 嗓音的；直言的，与 voice 同根
无声的，由 voice 加 -less 构成
浊音的，由 voice 加 -ed 构成

definition_zh: 音量；体积、容积；量、数额；（书的）卷、册
definition_en: the loudness of sound; the amount of space something fills; a quantity; one book of a set
core_image: 旋钮拧大的一格：同一台机器，装下更多、响过更多
scene: 深夜的书房里，他把收音机的旋钮轻轻拧小。Please turn down the volume.
sceneCN: 这里 volume 是「音量」（第 1 个义项：声音的大小）；句意为请把音量调低。一格一格拧动的旋钮，就是这个词。

pos.zh: 名词：音量；体积；量；卷册

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「容量的、按体积计的」，由 volume 加 -ric 构成
形容词，义为「体积大的；著述多的」，由同根加后缀构成
名词，义为「容积计」，较少使用

senses.title: Loudness of sound
senses.titleCN: 音量：声音的响度
senses.definition: how loud or soft a sound is
senses.definitionCN: 声音的大小强弱
senses.example: Please turn down the volume.
senses.exampleCN: 请把音量调低。
senses.why: A rolled scroll holds more; sound fills the room the way a roll fills space.
senses.whyCN: 成卷之物容纳更多；声音充满房间，正如卷轴充满空间。

senses.title: Space filled
senses.titleCN: 体积：占据的三维空间
senses.definition: the amount of three-dimensional space an object takes up
senses.definitionCN: 物体占据的三维空间大小
senses.example: The tank measures a volume of four cubic meters.
senses.exampleCN: 这个水箱的容积为四立方米。
senses.why: How much space a thing rolls out into is its volume.
senses.whyCN: 一件东西铺开占据多少空间，即是它的体积。

senses.title: Amount or quantity
senses.titleCN: 量：交易的数额或数量
senses.definition: the total amount or number of something, especially in business
senses.definitionCN: 某物的总量或总数，尤其用于商业
senses.example: Trade volume doubled after the new port opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新港口启用后贸易额翻了一番。
senses.why: Space becomes counting: how much flows through, like water through a channel.
senses.whyCN: 空间之量转为数目之量：流过多少，如水过渠道。

senses.title: A book of a set
senses.titleCN: 卷、册：成套书籍中的一本
senses.definition: one physical book, especially one of a multi-book work
senses.definitionCN: 一本实体书，尤指多卷本著作中的一册
senses.example: Volume three of the encyclopedia came out first.
senses.exampleCN: 这套百科全书的第三卷最先出版。
senses.why: Latin volumen is a rolled papyrus; books began as rolls, so a book keeps the roll's name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 volumen 指莎草纸卷；书起初就是卷轴，成册的书沿用了「卷」的名字。

intro.en: Volume comes from Latin volumen, a roll of writing, from volvere, to roll.
intro.cn: volume 源自拉丁语 volumen（书写纸卷），出自动词 volvere（滚动）。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wel- means to turn or roll, behind wheel and volvere alike.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wel- 意为转动或滚动，是 wheel 与 volvere 的共同来源。

items.en: Volvere means to roll; volumen is the thing rolled, a scroll of papyrus.
items.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 意为滚动；volumen 即卷起之物——莎草纸卷。

items.en: Volumen extends to any written work, since works were read in rolls.
items.cn: volumen 引申指任何成文著作，因当时著作以卷轴形式阅读。

items.en: The word becomes volum(e) in French, passing into English with the book sense.
items.cn: 该词在法语中作 volum(e)，带着「书卷」义进入英语。

items.en: English first uses volume for a book, then for bulk or capacity, and later for loudness with sound technology.
items.cn: 英语先指书册，再指体量与容量，随声学技术发展又指响度。

note.en: Look-alikes share the roll-root; near meanings cover amounts, sizes, and loudness.
note.cn: 形近组共享「滚动」词根，近义组涵盖数量、尺寸与响度。

entries.definition: large in bulk; writing much
entries.definitionCN: 体积庞大的；著述丰硕的；volume 的形容词形式

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from Latin volvere, to roll.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 volvere（滚动）。

normal.en: volvere means to roll; volumen is a rolled scroll of papyrus.
normal.cn: volvere 意为滚动；volumen 是卷起的莎草纸卷。

normal.en: involve is to roll something in; revolve is to roll again and again.
normal.cn: involve 是滚进去（卷入），revolve 是反复滚（旋转）。

normal.en: a set of books is still called volumes, one roll each.
normal.cn: 成套的书至今叫 volumes，一册即一卷。

normal.en: the volume knob rolls sound bigger or smaller.
normal.cn: 音量旋钮把声音「滚」大或滚小。

normal.en: voluminous describes a dress or a writer that takes much space.
normal.cn: voluminous 形容占空间大的裙摆或多产的作家。

abstract.en: A scroll unrolling across a desk: the space it claims is its volume.
abstract.cn: 桌上徐徐展开的卷轴：它占据的空间就是它的 volume。

abstract.en: A knob turning one notch at a time: the room grows quieter.
abstract.cn: 旋钮一格一格转动：房间渐渐安静。

abstract.en: Shelf after shelf of matching spines: ten volumes, one work.
abstract.cn: 书脊排成一列又一列：十卷书，一部著作。

examples.en: The engine's volume made conversation impossible.
examples.cn: 发动机的音量让人无法交谈。

examples.en: The factory raised its production volume last quarter.
examples.cn: 工厂上个季度提高了产量。

examples.en: Her diary filled five volumes before she turned thirty.
examples.cn: 三十岁前她的日记已写满五册。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我流目」——我放眼量出体积与音量；书一卷卷展开如流水铺目。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源来自拉丁 volumen（纸卷）。

root: 拉丁语 volvere（滚动）→ volumen（卷起之物、纸卷）→ 古法语 volum → 英语 volume。印欧词根 *wel-（重构形式）同时衍生 wheel、evolve、revolve 等。

sensesIntro.en: One rolled word grows four ways: the loudness that fills, the space that holds, the amount that flows, and the book that unrolls.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「卷」字四个方向生长：充满房间的响度、容纳的体积、流动的量、展开的书卷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the rolled thing claiming space
core.cn: 核心意象：卷起之物占据的空间

branches.en: The roll measured in three dimensions
branches.cn: 以三维度量的卷：体积

branches.en: The roll counted as it flows through
branches.cn: 流转中被计数的卷：数额

branches.en: The roll that fills a room with sound
branches.cn: 以声响充满房间的卷：音量

branches.en: The roll that became a book
branches.cn: 变成书的卷：册

branches.en: All three quantities answer one question: how much
branches.cn: 三种量回答同一个问题：有多少

intro.en: The roll-root turns through prefixes into some of the most common verbs in English.
intro.cn: 「滚动」词根加前缀，转出英语最常用的一批动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere rolls in every direction its prefixes point.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 随前缀指向各个方向滚动。

definition_zh: 自愿的；志愿的；无偿的；随意的；自愿做出的
definition_en: done, given, or chosen by your own free will, without being forced or paid
core_image: 自己伸出的手：没有人推，没有人付钱，是你自己决定做的
scene: 社区中心贴出新的招募海报，来往的人驻足细看。Attendance at the evening classes is entirely voluntary.
sceneCN: 这里 voluntary 是「自愿的」（第 1 个义项：出于自由意志、不受强制）；句意是晚间课程完全凭个人意愿参加，来去自由。

pos.zh: 形容词：自愿的；志愿的；无偿的；随意的
名词：即兴独奏曲（尤指管风琴）；自愿行动者

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「自愿地、主动地」，由形容词加副词后缀构成
名词，义为「志愿者」，与 voluntary 同出拉丁词根 voluntas
名词，义为「自愿性」，由形容词加抽象名词后缀构成
形容词，义为「不自愿的、无意的」，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成
副词，义为「不由自主地」，由 involuntary 加副词后缀构成

senses.title: Done by free will
senses.titleCN: 自愿的：出于自己的意愿
senses.definition: done or chosen by your own decision, without being forced
senses.definitionCN: 出于自己的决定而做，不受外界强迫
senses.example: Attendance at the evening classes is entirely voluntary.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间课程完全凭个人意愿参加。
senses.why: Latin voluntas means will or wish; the adjective marks action born of one's own will.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 voluntas 意为意志、意愿；这个形容词标记「由自己的意志而生」的行动。

senses.title: Unpaid and offered
senses.titleCN: 无偿的：不取报酬的付出
senses.definition: done without payment, especially for a charitable cause
senses.definitionCN: 不取报酬地去做，尤指为公益或慈善
senses.example: She does voluntary work at the local shelter every weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个周末都在当地收容所做志愿工作。
senses.why: What you will freely, you need not be paid for; giving time becomes giving it for free.
senses.whyCN: 出于自愿去做，便不要求回报，于是「自愿」延伸为「无偿」之义。

senses.title: Run by volunteers
senses.titleCN: 志愿的：由志愿者组成或运作
senses.definition: organized or staffed by people who work without pay
senses.definitionCN: 由不取报酬的人组成或运作的（组织、机构）
senses.example: The library survived thanks to the voluntary sector.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆得以维持，多亏志愿部门。
senses.why: Groups of willing people form a whole sector; the adjective names that collective choice.
senses.whyCN: 许多自愿者的集合构成一个部门，形容词转而指称这种集体的自愿组织。

senses.title: Under conscious control
senses.titleCN: 随意的：受意识支配的（身体动作）
senses.definition: controlled by conscious decision of the mind, as muscles or movements
senses.definitionCN: 由意识主动控制的，如肌肉或身体动作
senses.example: Breathing is partly voluntary and partly automatic.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸部分受意识控制，部分自动进行。
senses.why: Will governs the body's actions; movements you can choose are called voluntary.
senses.whyCN: 意志支配身体的行动，凡可由意识决定的动作即称「随意」。

senses.title: Not required by law
senses.titleCN: 非强制性的：法律或规章不做要求
senses.definition: not required by law or rules, but open to anyone who wishes
senses.definitionCN: 法律或规章不强制要求，愿意者可参与
senses.example: The company signed a voluntary code of conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 公司签署了一份自愿遵守的行为准则。
senses.why: Where force ends, will begins; what the law leaves free rests on voluntary choice.
senses.whyCN: 强制止步之处即意愿开始之处，法律不强制之事便依赖自愿选择。

senses.title: A free instrumental piece
senses.titleCN: 即兴独奏曲：尤指管风琴的自由演奏
senses.definition: a solo piece, especially for organ, played freely before or after a service
senses.definitionCN: 在礼拜前后自由演奏的独奏曲，尤指管风琴曲
senses.example: The organist opened the service with a short voluntary.
senses.exampleCN: 管风琴师以一首简短的即兴独奏曲开场。
senses.why: The player plays at will, without a set duty; freedom of will names the free piece.
senses.whyCN: 演奏者随兴而奏、无既定任务，「随意」之义转指这种自由演奏的乐曲。

intro.en: Voluntary comes from Latin voluntas, will or free choice, formed on the verb velle, to wish or to will.
intro.cn: voluntary 源自拉丁语 voluntas（意志、自愿的选择），该词由动词 velle（愿意、想要）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *welh₁- means to want or to choose, giving wish-words across Indo-European languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 *welh₁- 意为想要、选择，在各印欧语言中衍生出一族「意愿」词。

items.en: Velle means to wish; its noun voluntas means will, and the adjective voluntarius means of one's own will.
items.cn: 拉丁语 velle 意为愿意；名词 voluntas 意为意志，形容词 voluntarius 意为出于自己意志的。

items.en: The word passes into French as volontaire, keeping the sense of free choice.
items.cn: 该词以 volontaire 进入法语，保留自由选择之义。

items.en: English borrows voluntary in religious and legal writing, meaning done of one's own will.
items.cn: 英语在宗教与法律文本中借入 voluntary，意为出于本人意愿所为。

items.en: The senses of unpaid charitable work and of muscles under conscious control take hold.
items.cn: 17 至 19 世纪，「无偿公益」与「受意识控制的肌肉」两义确立。

items.en: Voluntary now names free choice everywhere, from voluntary work to the voluntary sector.
items.cn: 如今 voluntary 广泛指自愿之事，从志愿工作到志愿部门皆用此词。

note.en: Voluntary stands beside its Latin will-family and the opposite force-family; look-alikes share the root, near meanings share the field of willingness.
note.cn: voluntary 与拉丁「意志」词族及其反面「强制」词族相邻：形近组共享词根，近义组共享「自愿」义场。

entries.definition: a person who offers to do something without being paid
entries.definitionCN: 志愿者；与 voluntary 同出拉丁 voluntas，名词指自愿者

entries.definition: in a way done by free choice
entries.definitionCN: 自愿地；由 voluntary 加副词后缀构成

entries.definition: done against or without one's will
entries.definitionCN: 不自愿的、不由自主的；加否定前缀 in- 构成，义与本词相反

entries.definition: the principle of relying on voluntary action rather than state compulsion
entries.definitionCN: 自愿主义；由本词加 -ism 构成的学说名词

entries.definition: kind and wishing to do good
entries.definitionCN: 仁慈的、乐善的；同为 -ent/-lent 结尾，但词根是 velle 的另一形式 bene velle（愿意好），词族相关而拼写相异

entries.definition: ready and happy to do something
entries.definitionCN: 愿意的、乐意的；日耳曼词源，强调乐意的态度

entries.definition: available if you want it, but not required
entries.definitionCN: 可选择的、非强制的；侧重「可选」，不侧重「无偿」

entries.definition: done or kept without payment
entries.definitionCN: 无报酬的；只描述无酬，不强调意愿

entries.definition: happening naturally, without being planned
entries.definitionCN: 自发的；强调未经计划，voluntary 强调自由决定

entries.definition: required by a rule or law
entries.definitionCN: 强制的、义务的；与本词构成直接反义对照

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin will-family of voluntas and velle.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 voluntas（意志）与 velle（愿意）词族。

normal.en: velle means to wish; voluntary means done by your own wish.
normal.cn: velle 意为愿意；voluntary 就是「按自己的意愿做」。

normal.en: volunteer is the person form: one who offers freely.
normal.cn: volunteer 是它的「人」形：主动报名、不计报酬的人。

normal.en: involuntary adds the negative in-, meaning against your will.
normal.cn: involuntary 加否定前缀 in-，意为「违背意愿、不由自主」。

normal.en: voluntarily is simply voluntary in action: doing it by choice.
normal.cn: voluntarily 就是 voluntary 的动作版：自愿地去做。

normal.en: the word sits inside voluntary sector, the world of unpaid help.
normal.cn: 这个词就住在 voluntary sector（志愿部门）里，即无偿奉献的世界。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand reaching out on its own, pushed by nobody and paid by nobody.
abstract.cn: 想象一只自己伸出的手，无人推动，无人付钱。

abstract.en: Two doors stand open: one says forced, one says chosen; you walk through the second.
abstract.cn: 两扇门都开着：一扇写着强制，一扇写着自愿；你走向第二扇。

abstract.en: A will like a small engine inside the chest, starting the action before anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 意志像胸中一台小引擎，不等任何人开口就先发动了行动。

examples.en: He joined the rescue team on a purely voluntary basis.
examples.cn: 他完全出于自愿加入了救援队。

examples.en: The hospital relies heavily on voluntary donations.
examples.cn: 这家医院在很大程度上依赖志愿捐助。

examples.en: Smiling is usually voluntary, but laughter often is not.
examples.cn: 微笑通常是随意的，大笑却往往身不由己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我乐于停」——我乐于停下被强迫的脚步，自己选择去做，这才是自愿。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 voluntas（意志）。

root: 拉丁语 velle（愿意）+ 名词 voluntas（意志）+ 形容词后缀 -arius 构成 voluntarius，经古法语 volontaire 进入英语。同根词还有 volunteer、benevolent（bene 好 + velle）、malevolent（male 坏 + velle）等，「意愿」一族。

sensesIntro.en: From the will outward: free choice, free giving, volunteer groups, the body's chosen movements, and the free piece of music.
sensesIntro.cn: 从意愿向外铺开：自由选择、无偿付出、志愿组织、身体受控的动作，最后到随兴的乐曲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one act of will, from inner wish outward to free action
core.cn: 核心意象：同一次「意愿」，从内心的想延伸到自由的做

branches.en: The root sense: acting by your own decision
branches.cn: 根本义：按自己的决定行动

branches.en: Willingness without wages: charity and the volunteer sector
branches.cn: 不取报酬的意愿：公益与志愿部门

branches.en: Will applied to the body: movements under conscious control
branches.cn: 意志作用于身体：受意识支配的动作

branches.en: Where law stays silent, will fills the gap
branches.cn: 法律沉默之处，由意愿来填补

branches.en: Playing at will becomes the free musical piece
branches.cn: 随兴而奏，便成为自由的乐曲

intro.en: The Latin will-verbs velle and its noun voluntas spread through prefixes of good, bad, and negation.
intro.cn: 拉丁语意愿动词 velle 及其名词 voluntas，借助「好、坏、否定」等前缀铺成一族词。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, velle built a family of words about wishing well, ill, or freely.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，velle 构成了一族关于「愿好、愿坏、愿自便」的词。

definition_zh: 投票；表决；选举；投票权；得票数
definition_en: to express your choice in an election or decision by formally marking a ballot or raising a hand
core_image: 举起的手和纸上的勾：把你的选择放进所有人的选择里一起数
scene: 会场安静下来，主持人宣布开始表决。Every member has one vote in the annual meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 vote 是「投票权」（第 4 个义项：一名成员所拥有的那一份表决权）；句意是年会上每位成员都有一票。

pos.zh: 名词：投票；表决；选票；得票数；投票权
动词：投票；表决；选举；投票通过

名词，义为「选票」，义场相邻的名词

senses.title: To express a formal choice
senses.titleCN: 投票：用规定方式表达选择
senses.definition: to mark a ballot or otherwise formally show whom or what you support
senses.definitionCN: 在选票上做记号或以其他规定方式表明你支持的人或提案
senses.example: Millions of citizens voted in the national election.
senses.exampleCN: 数百万公民在全国大选中投了票。
senses.why: Latin votum means a vow or wish; a formal choice is a wish made publicly and countably.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 votum 意为誓愿；正式的选择就是把愿望公开说出、可以被统计。

senses.title: To decide by collective choice
senses.titleCN: 表决：由集体共同决定
senses.definition: to reach a group decision by counting everyone's choices
senses.definitionCN: 通过统计每个人的选择来作出集体决定
senses.example: The committee voted to postpone the project.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会表决决定推迟该项目。
senses.why: Many wishes are laid side by side and counted; the largest one becomes the decision.
senses.whyCN: 把众人的愿望并列在一起计数，占多数的那个便成为决定。

senses.title: A single choice cast
senses.titleCN: 选票：一份投出的选择
senses.definition: an act or piece of paper showing one person's choice in an election
senses.definitionCN: 表明一个人在选举中选择的动作或那张纸
senses.example: She put her vote into the ballot box and left.
senses.exampleCN: 她把选票投入票箱，然后离开。
senses.why: Each wish becomes one unit to be counted; the unit itself is a vote.
senses.whyCN: 每个愿望化作一个可数的单位，这个单位本身就是一张选票。

senses.title: The right to take part
senses.titleCN: 投票权：参与表决的资格
senses.definition: the right that a person or member has to take part in a decision
senses.definitionCN: 个人或成员参与决定所拥有的资格
senses.example: Every member has one vote in the annual meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 年会上每位成员都有一票。
senses.why: If a wish counts, that counting is a right; having one wish means having one vote.
senses.whyCN: 愿望若被统计，这种被统计就是一项权利；有一份愿望即有一票。

senses.title: The total or result counted
senses.titleCN: 得票数：统计出来的总数
senses.definition: the total number of choices recorded in an election or ballot
senses.definitionCN: 选举或表决中记录到的选择总数
senses.example: The final vote gave the mayor a second term.
senses.exampleCN: 最终计票结果让市长获得连任。
senses.why: Counted wishes add up to a number; that number names the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 被计数的愿望累加为数字，这个数字就代表结果。

senses.title: To approve or choose by ballot
senses.titleCN: 投票选出：用投票方式认可或选出
senses.definition: to choose someone or approve something through a formal ballot
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式投票选出某人或通过某事
senses.example: The players voted her captain of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 队员们投票选她当队长。
senses.why: The collective wish is aimed at a person; choosing becomes electing.
senses.whyCN: 集体的愿望指向一个人，选择便成为选举。

intro.en: Vote descends from Latin votum, a vow or solemn wish, the past participle of vovere, to promise solemnly.
intro.cn: vote 源自拉丁语 votum（誓愿、庄重的愿望），它是动词 vovere（郑重许诺）的过去分词。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ewegwh- or a related form means to speak solemnly or vow; the exact shape is generally agreed only within Latin.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根与「郑重言说、许愿」相关，其确切形态仅在拉丁语内部较有共识。

items.en: Vovere means to vow; votum is what is vowed, a wish dedicated to the gods.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vovere 意为许愿；votum 是许下的愿，即献给神明的愿望。

items.en: Votum extends from religious wishes to any solemnly expressed choice or opinion.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，votum 从宗教誓愿扩展为任何郑重表达的愿望或意见。

items.en: English takes vote from the Latin participle, first as a solemn wish, then as an expressed opinion.
items.cn: 英语直接取自拉丁语分词形式的 vote，先指庄重的愿望，后指表达出的意见。

items.en: The political sense hardens: a vote becomes a counted choice in parliament and elections.
items.cn: 17 世纪政治义定型：vote 成为议会与选举中可被统计的选择。

items.en: Vote now covers casting ballots, electing leaders, and counting the results in any assembly.
items.cn: 如今 vote 涵盖投票、选人、计票，适用于各种集会与选举。

note.en: Vote belongs to the Latin vow-family and the election word-field; look-alikes share the vow-root or spelling, near meanings share the field of choosing.
note.cn: vote 与拉丁「誓愿」词族及选举义场相邻：形近组共享誓愿词根或拼形，近义组共享「选择」义场。

entries.definition: the power to reject a decision; to reject it
entries.definitionCN: 否决（权）；源自拉丁语，字面为「我不许」，与 vote 同出「愿」词族但方向相反

entries.definition: to give time, love, or energy to something
entries.definitionCN: 奉献、专注于；由 de- 加 vovere 词根构成，义为郑重许下

entries.definition: offered or done as a vow or wish
entries.definitionCN: 还愿的、许愿的；与 vote 同根的形容词，属宗教用词

entries.definition: a paper or system used for voting
entries.definitionCN: 选票、投票制；与 vote 只是义场相接，词源是意大利语的小纸球，拼写易混但词源不同

entries.definition: careful not to confuse vote with veto: one chooses, one rejects
entries.definitionCN: vote 与 veto 仅一字母之差：一个选择，一个否决；devoted 则属同根词，词形相近易混

entries.definition: a system, paper, or act of secret voting
entries.definitionCN: 选票、无记名投票；强调投票的形式

entries.definition: to choose someone for a position by voting
entries.definitionCN: 选举、推选；强调选出人担任职位

entries.definition: the process of voting, or a survey of opinions
entries.definitionCN: 投票；也指民意调查，侧重统计人数

entries.definition: a direct public vote on a single question
entries.definitionCN: 全民公投；针对单一议题的直接投票

entries.definition: to choose not to vote
entries.definitionCN: 弃权；与投票相对的选择

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin vow-family of vovere and votum.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 vovere（许愿）与 votum（誓愿）词族。

normal.en: vovere means to vow; voting is your wish said out loud and counted.
normal.cn: vovere 意为许愿；投票就是把愿望说出来并被人计数。

normal.en: devote is the same root: to vow yourself to something.
normal.cn: devote 同根：把自己许诺给某事。

normal.en: veto keeps the first-person Latin shape: I forbid, the opposite of choosing.
normal.cn: veto 保留拉丁第一人称形态：我不许，恰是选择的反面。

normal.en: voter is the person who turns a wish into a counted choice.
normal.cn: voter 是把愿望变成一张被计数选票的人。

normal.en: cast a vote is the fixed phrase: throwing your wish onto the pile.
normal.cn: cast a vote 是固定搭配：把你的愿望投进那一堆里。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl where every hand drops one stone: the tallest pile is the decision.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗，每只手投进一颗石子：堆得最高的那边就是决定。

abstract.en: A wish whispered to a god in Rome becomes a card dropped in a box today.
abstract.cn: 古罗马对神低声许下的愿，如今变成投进箱中的一张卡。

abstract.en: One voice alone is faint; counted together, voices become a verdict.
abstract.cn: 一个声音很微弱，加在一起被计数，声音便成为裁决。

examples.en: Employees voted for a shorter working week.
examples.cn: 员工们投票赞成缩短每周工时。

examples.en: The bill passed by a narrow vote in the senate.
examples.cn: 该法案在参议院以微弱的票数差距获得通过。

examples.en: Who did you vote for in the last election?
examples.cn: 上次选举你投了谁的票？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我投」——vote 的发音就像「我投」，我投出我的一票。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 votum（誓愿）。

root: 拉丁语 vovere（郑重许诺、许愿）+ 过去分词 votum（誓愿）进入英语，先义为愿望、意见，后义为投票。同根词 devote（奉献）、devout（虔诚的）、votive（还愿的）同出一族，核心是「郑重表达愿望」。

sensesIntro.en: From one solemn wish to a counted collective verdict: cast it, count it, and the result decides.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一份郑重的愿望到被计数的集体裁决：投出、计数，结果由多数决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one wish made formal, joined with all wishes and counted
core.cn: 核心意象：一份愿望被正式化，与所有愿望汇合并计数

branches.en: The individual act: one wish formally cast
branches.cn: 个体行为：一份愿望被正式投出

branches.en: The group act: choosing and approving together
branches.cn: 群体行为：共同选择与认可

branches.en: The standing right to be counted
branches.cn: 被计数的资格：投票权

branches.en: The number that the wishes add up to
branches.cn: 愿望累加出的数字：得票数

branches.en: The verdict: from counting to naming a winner
branches.cn: 裁决：从计数到宣布结果

intro.en: The vow-verbs of Latin spread through prefixes that add the wish toward, away, or upward.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的许愿动词借助前缀，把愿望引向不同方向：奉献、转向、许上。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, vovere built a family of words about solemn wishes, sacred or personal.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，vovere 构成了一族关于郑重愿望的词，或神圣或个人。

definition_zh: 易受伤害的；脆弱的；易受攻击的；易患病的
definition_en: easily hurt, attacked, or harmed, either physically or emotionally
core_image: 露出的伤口：护甲裂开一道缝，谁碰谁疼
scene: 暴雨中，帐篷的绳结松脱了。The old bridge is vulnerable to flooding after heavy rain.
sceneCN: 这里 vulnerable 是「易受伤害的」（第 1 个义项：容易受到损害）；句意是暴雨之后，这座旧桥容易被洪水破坏。

pos.zh: 形容词：易受伤害的；脆弱的；易受攻击的；易患病的

collocations.zh: 使某人处于易受伤害的境地

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「脆弱性、易受伤害性」，由形容词加抽象名词后缀构成
形容词，义为「无法伤害的、刀枪不入的」，由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成
副词，义为「脆弱地」，由形容词加副词后缀构成

senses.title: Easily harmed physically
senses.titleCN: 易受伤害的：容易受到物理损害
senses.definition: easily damaged or hurt by physical forces or events
senses.definitionCN: 容易被物理力量或事件损害
senses.example: The old bridge is vulnerable to flooding after heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨之后，这座旧桥容易被洪水破坏。
senses.why: Latin vulnus means a wound; a woundable thing is one harm can reach.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vulnus 意为伤口；可受伤之物就是伤害能够抵达的东西。

senses.title: Weak against attack
senses.titleCN: 易受攻击的：防御上存在弱点
senses.definition: open to being attacked or criticized, with weak defenses
senses.definitionCN: 防御薄弱，容易受到攻击或批评
senses.example: The network was vulnerable because one server had no password.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网络很脆弱，因为一台服务器没设密码。
senses.why: Where armor has a gap, the blow lands; the wound-word names the reachable spot.
senses.whyCN: 护甲有缝之处打击便能命中，「伤口」一词正指向那个可及之处。

senses.title: Emotionally exposed
senses.titleCN: 情感上脆弱的：内心容易受伤
senses.definition: easily hurt in feelings, or willing to show feelings openly
senses.definitionCN: 情感上容易受伤，或愿意坦诚展露内心
senses.example: She felt vulnerable talking about her childhood in public.
senses.exampleCN: 她当众谈起童年时，感到内心脆弱而暴露。
senses.why: The heart can be wounded as the body can; the metaphor moves from skin to soul.
senses.whyCN: 心也会像身体一样受伤，比喻由皮肤延伸到灵魂。

senses.title: At risk in a population
senses.titleCN: 易患病的：身体上易受疾病侵袭
senses.definition: at risk of catching a disease or being harmed by conditions
senses.definitionCN: 容易患病或被不良条件伤害的（人群、个体）
senses.example: Babies and the elderly are especially vulnerable to the virus.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿和老人特别容易感染这种病毒。
senses.why: A body already weak takes wounds sooner; susceptibility is woundedness waiting.
senses.whyCN: 已经虚弱的身体更容易受伤，易感性就是「等着发生的伤口」。

senses.title: In a weak social position
senses.titleCN: 弱势的：社会处境容易受损害
senses.definition: in a position of disadvantage where harm or loss is more likely
senses.definitionCN: 处于不利地位、更容易受到损失或伤害的
senses.example: Voluntary groups protect vulnerable members of society.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿组织保护社会中的弱势成员。
senses.why: Without resources, armor, or allies, every blow reaches the person beneath.
senses.whyCN: 缺少资源、防护与盟友，每一记打击都能直接落到那个人身上。

intro.en: Vulnerable comes from Latin vulnus, a wound, probably related to vellere, to pluck or tear, though the exact link is generally believed rather than proven.
intro.cn: vulnerable 源自拉丁语 vulnus（伤口），一般认为与 vellere（拔、撕扯）相关，但确切联系属于普遍推定而非定论。

items.en: The reconstructed root behind vellere means to tear or pluck; its connection to the wound-word is a commonly accepted hypothesis.
items.cn: vellere 背后的重构词根意为撕扯、拔取；它与「伤口」一词的联系是普遍接受的假说。

items.en: Vulnus means a wound; the adjective vulnerabilis means able to be wounded.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vulnus 意为伤口；形容词 vulnerabilis 意为可被弄伤的。

items.en: Vulnerabilis passes into late Latin usage as a descriptive term for anything woundable.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，vulnerabilis 用作描述任何可受伤之物的词语。

items.en: English borrows vulnerable in military writing first, for cities and troops open to attack.
items.cn: 英语最初在军事文本中借入 vulnerable，指易受攻击的城市与军队。

items.en: The sense spreads to emotional hurt and to people exposed to disease or hardship.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，词义扩展到情感伤害及易患病、易受困的人群。

items.en: Vulnerable now names weak points everywhere, from vulnerable groups to vulnerable software.
items.cn: 如今 vulnerable 指一切薄弱之处，从弱势群体到有漏洞的软件。

note.en: Vulnerable stands beside its Latin wound-family and the risk word-field; look-alikes share the root, near meanings share the field of exposure to harm.
note.cn: vulnerable 与拉丁「伤口」词族及「风险」义场相邻：形近组共享词根，近义组共享「暴露于伤害」义场。

entries.definition: impossible to harm or attack successfully
entries.definitionCN: 刀枪不入的、无法伤害的；加否定前缀 in- 构成，义与本词相反

entries.definition: the quality of being easily hurt, or a specific weak point
entries.definitionCN: 脆弱性、漏洞；由 vulnerable 加抽象名词后缀构成

entries.definition: an injury caused by a weapon; to inflict such an injury
entries.definitionCN: 伤口、使受伤；日耳曼词源，与 vulnerable 义场相邻但词源不同，拼写易混

entries.definition: a large bird that feeds on carrion
entries.definitionCN: 秃鹫；与本词开头字母相同、易在拼写上混淆，但词源完全不同

entries.definition: lacking refinement, or relating to ordinary people
entries.definitionCN: 粗俗的、大众的；词首拼形相近，源自 vulgus（民众），词源不同

entries.definition: left without cover or protection
entries.definitionCN: 暴露的、无遮蔽的；强调缺少保护这一状态

entries.definition: easily broken or damaged
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的、脆弱的；侧重物体易碎，vulnerable 兼指人

entries.definition: easily affected by something, such as disease or influence
entries.definitionCN: 易受影响的、易感染的；侧重易感性

entries.definition: having no way to protect yourself
entries.definitionCN: 毫无防备的、手无寸铁的；强调没有防御手段

entries.definition: in danger of being harmed
entries.definitionCN: 处于危险中的；口语与官方文件常用的短语式近义

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin wound-family of vulnus.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自拉丁语 vulnus（伤口）词族。

normal.en: vulnus means wound; vulnerable literally means wound-able.
normal.cn: vulnus 意为伤口；vulnerable 字面就是「可受伤的」。

normal.en: invulnerable flips it with in-: wound-proof, like armor.
normal.cn: invulnerable 用 in- 反转它：防伤的，如同铠甲。

normal.en: vulnerability is the noun: the state of being woundable.
normal.cn: vulnerability 是它的名词形式：可受伤这种状态。

normal.en: the stress of the word sits on the first syllable: VUL-nerable.
normal.cn: 这个词的重音在第一个音节：VUL-nerable。

normal.en: the phrase vulnerable to something is the common frame: open to that harm.
normal.cn: 常见搭配 vulnerable to something：对那种伤害敞开着。

abstract.en: Picture armor with one cracked seam: light, rain, and hands all find it.
abstract.cn: 想象护甲上裂开的一道缝：光线、雨水、他人之手都能找到它。

abstract.en: A peeled fruit in an open market: anything may touch it first.
abstract.cn: 市场上削了皮的水果：谁都可能先碰到它。

abstract.en: Saying a secret out loud makes the chest a wound the world can enter.
abstract.cn: 把秘密说出口的那一刻，胸膛便成了世界可以进入的伤口。

examples.en: Young birds are vulnerable to predators until they can fly.
examples.cn: 幼鸟在学会飞行之前容易受捕食者伤害。

examples.en: He became emotionally vulnerable after the divorce.
examples.cn: 离婚之后，他在情感上变得脆弱。

examples.en: The report listed vulnerable coastal towns facing rising seas.
examples.cn: 报告列出了面临海平面上升、易受损害的沿海城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我呢弱」——「我呢？弱呀。」护甲裂开一道缝时先承认自己弱，才能补上它。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 vulnus（伤口）。

root: 拉丁语 vulnus（伤口）+ 形容词后缀 -abilis（可……的）构成 vulnerabilis（可被弄伤的），经晚期拉丁语进入英语。一般认为 vulnus 与动词 vellere（拔、撕扯）同源，但这一联系属于推定。同族词 invulnerable（加否定前缀 in-）、vulnerability 等。

sensesIntro.en: From the open wound outward: physical harm, weak defenses, exposed feelings, disease risk, and social disadvantage.
sensesIntro.cn: 从敞开的伤口向外铺开：物理损害、防御弱点、暴露的情感、患病风险，最后到社会处境的弱势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one open gap where harm can reach what it could not before
core.cn: 核心意象：一道敞开的缺口，伤害由此能够抵达原本够不到的地方

branches.en: Bodies and things that harm reaches first
branches.cn: 伤害最先抵达的身体与事物

branches.en: The reachable gap in walls, systems, and arguments
branches.cn: 城墙、系统与论证中可被攻入的缺口

branches.en: The heart with its guard down
branches.cn: 卸下防备的心灵

branches.en: People without armor of resources or allies
branches.cn: 缺少资源与盟友之甲的人们

branches.en: Where weakness meets intention, attack begins
branches.cn: 薄弱遇上恶意，攻击便开始

intro.en: The wound-root of Latin pairs with ability and negation suffixes to say who can and cannot be hurt.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「伤口」词根与「能够」「否定」等后缀组合，说明谁能与谁不能被伤害。

latinIntro.en: In Latin, vulnus gave both the wound noun and its derived adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 在拉丁语中，vulnus 既给出伤口这个名词，也派生出它的形容词。
