definition_zh: 工资；工钱；报酬；发动（战争、运动等）
definition_en: money paid regularly for work, usually by the hour or day; to start and carry on a war or campaign
core_image: 掌心里数好的钱：干一天活，换一天的钱
scene: 面包房打烊，老板从围裙口袋里掏出小信封。The workers demanded a fair wage for their extra hours.
sceneCN: 这里 wage 是「工资」（第 1 个义项：按时间计的劳动报酬）；句意是工人们要求额外工时获得公平的报酬。

pos.zh: 名词：工资；工钱；报酬
动词：发动；进行（战争、运动、斗争）

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「赌注」，与 wage 同出一源，指押上的「承诺之物」
名词复数形式，常特指按周或日结算的体力劳动报酬
形容词，义为「领薪水的」，由过去分词转作定语

senses.title: Payment for work by time
senses.titleCN: 工资：按时间计算的劳动报酬
senses.definition: money paid regularly for labor, usually calculated by the hour or day
senses.definitionCN: 按小时或天数定期支付给劳动者的钱
senses.example: The workers demanded a fair wage for their extra hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求额外的工时获得公平的报酬。
senses.why: Old English wedd meant a pledge; promised payment for a day's work became the wage.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wedd 意为保证、承诺；为一天劳动承诺的钱就成了工资。

senses.title: Reward or recompense
senses.titleCN: 报酬：行为的报偿或代价
senses.definition: a reward or deserved return for something done, often figurative
senses.definitionCN: 对所做之事的报偿或应得的回报，常用于比喻
senses.example: Peace of mind was the wages of her long patience.
senses.exampleCN: 内心的安宁是她长久耐心的报偿。
senses.why: Whatever is pledged in return for deeds can be paid in more than money.
senses.whyCN: 凡为行为承诺过的回报，可以不止用金钱来支付。

senses.title: To carry on a struggle
senses.titleCN: 发动：开始并进行一场斗争
senses.definition: to start and continue a war, campaign, or organized struggle
senses.definitionCN: 发动并持续进行战争、运动或有组织的斗争
senses.example: The city waged a long campaign against litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市发起了一场长期的反垃圾运动。
senses.why: A pledge made to fight becomes the fight itself; the promise turns into action.
senses.whyCN: 为战斗许下的承诺最终成了战斗本身，承诺化为行动。

senses.title: Wages as the income class
senses.titleCN: 工薪：以工资为生的阶层视角
senses.definition: payment for work considered as a class of income, as opposed to salary or profit
senses.definitionCN: 作为收入类别看待的劳动报酬，区别于薪金或利润
senses.example: Wages and prices rose together that decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那十年里工资和物价一同上涨。
senses.why: Counting pay in hours makes it a social category, not just a private sum.
senses.whyCN: 按时计酬使工资成为一种社会类别，而不只是一笔私人钱款。

intro.en: Wage descends through Old North French from Old English and Frankish roots meaning a pledge or surety.
intro.cn: wage 经古北方法语上溯至古英语与法兰克语词根，意为保证、担保。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wadi- means a pledge or security, something handed over as a promise.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wadi- 意为保证、抵押物，即作为承诺而交出的东西。

items.en: Wedd means a pledge or surety; related forms appear across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古英语 wedd 意为承诺、担保，同源形式见于各日耳曼语。

items.en: The Frankish loan becomes wage in Norman French, meaning a pledge and then payment.
items.cn: 法兰克语借词进入诺曼法语作 wage，先指担保，后指酬金。

items.en: Middle English takes wage as payment pledged for service, especially daily work.
items.cn: 中古英语取 wage 为劳务的应许报酬，尤指按日结算的工钱。

items.en: The verb sense of waging war grows from the pledge to carry a fight through.
items.cn: 15 至 16 世纪，wage 的动词义由「承诺作战到底」发展为「发动战争」。

items.en: Wage now names hourly pay and any sustained campaign, from minimum wage to waging peace.
items.cn: 如今 wage 既指时薪，也指任何持续的行动，从最低工资到发动的运动。

note.en: Wage sits beside its Germanic pledge-family and the pay word-field; look-alikes share the pledge-root, near meanings share the field of reward.
note.cn: wage 与日耳曼「担保」词族及「报酬」义场相邻：形近组共享担保词根，近义组共享报偿义场。

entries.definition: a bet; to bet money on an outcome
entries.definitionCN: 赌注、打赌；与 wage 同出「担保」词根，指押上的承诺

entries.definition: regular payment for work, plural form
entries.definitionCN: 工钱（复数形式）；历史上连带的 -s 曾被误作复数后缀

entries.definition: a piece of wood or metal with a pointed edge for splitting things
entries.definitionCN: 楔子；与 wage 仅一字母之差，词源不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: something pledged as a guarantee, especially in old texts
entries.definitionCN: 抵押物、挑战信物；古语用词，与 wage 同源变体

entries.definition: to promise, involve, or hire; to enter into conflict
entries.definitionCN: 使承诺、雇佣、交战；由法语 en- 加 gage（担保）构成

entries.definition: fixed regular payment, usually monthly and for professional work
entries.definitionCN: 薪金；按月固定，多指白领职位的报酬

entries.definition: money received for work, general term
entries.definitionCN: 报酬的总称；不区分结算方式

entries.definition: all money received, from any source
entries.definitionCN: 收入；范围更大，不限于劳动所得

entries.definition: an amount of money paid for something
entries.definitionCN: 付款、款项；指单笔支付而非定期报酬

entries.definition: money paid for a service or a professional's time
entries.definitionCN: 服务费、酬金；按事项或专业服务收取

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Germanic pledge-family behind wage.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自 wage 背后的日耳曼「担保」词族。

normal.en: the root means a pledge: a wage is pay promised in advance.
normal.cn: 词根意为担保：wage 是事先承诺好的报酬。

normal.en: wager keeps the same pledge: money staked on a promise.
normal.cn: wager 保留同一担保义：押在承诺上的钱。

normal.en: engage is en- plus gage: bound by a pledge.
normal.cn: engage 是 en- 加 gage：被承诺所约束。

normal.en: wage war grew from the pledge to carry a fight through.
normal.cn: wage war 源于「承诺把战斗打到底」。

normal.en: minimum wage is the fixed phrase everyone meets first.
normal.cn: minimum wage（最低工资）是人人最先遇到的固定搭配。

abstract.en: A hand opens at dusk and coins promised at dawn finally land in it.
abstract.cn: 黄昏摊开的手掌，接住清晨便许下的硬币。

abstract.en: A stamped pledge-paper turns into a small weekly envelope of coins.
abstract.cn: 盖了印的承诺书，变成每周一只装着硬币的小信封。

abstract.en: Promising a fight is already fighting: the pledge marches forward.
abstract.cn: 许诺一战便已在作战：承诺本身向前行进。

examples.en: The factory raised the hourly wage last spring.
examples.cn: 工厂去年春天提高了时薪。

examples.en: They waged a tireless campaign for cleaner rivers.
examples.cn: 他们发起了一场为清洁河流而奋斗的不懈运动。

examples.en: He lives on the wages from two part-time jobs.
examples.cn: 他靠两份兼职的工资生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂给」——工钱是雇主「喂给」工人的口粮，一天一喂。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自日耳曼语的「担保、承诺」。

root: 日耳曼语系词根 *wadi-（保证、抵押）→ 古英语 wedd（承诺、担保）→ 古法兰克语借入诺曼法语 wage（担保→酬金）→ 中古英语 wage。同族词有 wager（赌注）、gage（抵押物）、engage（en- + gage，使受承诺约束）。核心是「为承诺而交出的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: From the pledge outward: promised pay, earned reward, the pledge to fight, and wages as a social income class.
sensesIntro.cn: 从担保向外铺开：承诺的工钱、应得的报偿、作战的承诺，最后到作为社会收入类别的工薪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pledge handed over, first as pay, then as battle joined
core.cn: 核心意象：一份被交出的承诺，先是报酬，后是投入的战斗

branches.en: The root sense: payment pledged for work by the hour
branches.cn: 根本义：按时计酬的承诺报酬

branches.en: Reward beyond money: what deeds deserve
branches.cn: 超出金钱的报偿：行为应得之物

branches.en: Pay counted socially: wages as a class of income
branches.cn: 社会视角的报酬：作为收入类别的工薪

branches.en: The pledge to fight becomes the fight itself
branches.cn: 作战的承诺化为战斗本身

branches.en: Carrying a struggle through, from war to campaigns
branches.cn: 把斗争进行到底，从战争到运动

intro.en: The Germanic pledge-root spreads into English largely through French borrowings of the same Frankish word.
intro.cn: 日耳曼「担保」词根主要通过法语对同一法兰克词的借用进入英语。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic rather than Latin; French took it from Frankish speech.
latinIntro.cn: 这一词族属日耳曼而非拉丁来源；法语是从法兰克语中借入它的。

derivatives.zh: 赌注，与 wage 同根的名词
领薪水的，由过去分词转作定语
使承诺、雇佣，由法语 en- 加 gage 构成

definition_zh: 等待；等候；等待的时间；伺候进餐；等着到来
definition_en: to stay in a place or delay action until something happens or someone arrives
core_image: 坐在长椅上望着门口：时间走过，你留在原地不动
scene: 雨越下越大，乘客们缩在站台尽头。The delayed train finally came, and the passengers' long wait was over.
sceneCN: 这里 wait 是「等待的时间」（第 3 个义项：等待持续的那段时光）；句意是晚点的列车终于进站，乘客们漫长的等待结束了。

pos.zh: 动词：等待；等候；推迟行动；伺候进餐
名词：等待；等候的时间

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「侍者、服务员」，由动词加施动者后缀构成
名词，义为「女服务员」，由 waiter 加阴性后缀构成
名词，义为「等候、等待的状态」，由动词加动名词后缀构成

senses.title: To stay until something happens
senses.titleCN: 等待：停留至某事发生
senses.definition: to stay in place or delay acting until the expected thing occurs
senses.definitionCN: 停留在原地或暂不行动，直到所期待的事发生
senses.example: We waited on the platform until the fog lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在站台上一直等到雾散。
senses.why: Old North French waitier meant to watch; watching attentively became waiting for what you watch for.
senses.whyCN: 古北方法语 waitier 意为注视；聚精会神地看，便成了守候所盼之事。

senses.title: To be ready and available
senses.titleCN: 备好待命：随时可以提供服务
senses.definition: to be ready to be used, served, or taken
senses.definitionCN: 处于备好、可用、待人取用或服务的状态
senses.example: A hot meal was waiting for the travelers.
senses.exampleCN: 一顿热饭正等着赶路的人们。
senses.why: One who watches for guests stands ready; readiness is standing wait.
senses.whyCN: 守候客人的人随时准备着，待命状态就是「站着等候」。

senses.title: A period of staying
senses.titleCN: 等待的时间：等候持续的那段时光
senses.definition: an act or period of waiting; the time spent waiting
senses.definitionCN: 等待这一行为或它持续的时间
senses.example: The delayed train finally came, and the passengers' long wait was over.
senses.exampleCN: 晚点的列车终于进站，乘客们漫长的等待结束了。
senses.why: The act of watching-and-holding still can be named and even counted in minutes.
senses.whyCN: 守候不动这一行为本身可以被命名，甚至以分钟计数。

senses.title: To serve at table
senses.titleCN: 伺候进餐：为人端菜上桌
senses.definition: to serve food and drink to people at their tables
senses.definitionCN: 在餐桌旁为客人端送食物和饮品
senses.example: He waits tables at a bistro near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他在河边一家小酒馆当服务员。
senses.why: One who watches for guests' needs attends them; watching becomes serving.
senses.whyCN: 留心客人所需便是照应他们，注视之义转为伺候之义。

senses.title: To delay out of patience or hope
senses.titleCN: 暂缓：出于耐心或希望而推迟行动
senses.definition: to hold back action, often in hope that circumstances will improve
senses.definitionCN: 暂不采取行动，常怀有情况会好转的希望
senses.example: She decided to wait before answering the offer.
senses.exampleCN: 她决定先缓一缓，再答复那份邀约。
senses.why: Holding still while watching is also holding back one's own action.
senses.whyCN: 注视时保持不动，也包括按住自己不去行动。

intro.en: Wait comes from Old North French waitier, to watch or be watchful, of Germanic origin, related to the same family as wake.
intro.cn: wait 源自古北方法语 waitier（注视、留神），属日耳曼来源，与 wake 同族相关。

items.en: The reconstructed root *waht- means to be awake or watchful, the same family as wake and watch.
items.cn: 重构词根 *waht- 意为醒着、警觉，与 wake、watch 同族。

items.en: Waitier means to watch, to keep guard; the Germanic word lives on in Norman speech.
items.cn: 古北方法语 waitier 意为注视、看守；这一日耳曼词在诺曼语中留存。

items.en: Middle English borrows waiten meaning to watch, lie in ambush, or keep guard.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 waiten，意为注视、埋伏、看守。

items.en: The sense shifts from watching to staying until the watched thing comes.
items.cn: 14 至 15 世纪，词义由「注视」转为「留驻到所盼之事到来」。

items.en: The service sense grows: to attend on guests, and later to serve at table.
items.cn: 16 世纪服务义生长：先指侍奉宾客，后指在餐桌旁服务。

items.en: Wait now covers staying, pausing, waiting lines, and waiting tables alike.
items.cn: 如今 wait 涵盖停留、暂缓、排队等候与端盘子服务。

note.en: Wait stands beside its watchful Germanic family and the time word-field; look-alikes share the watch-root, near meanings share the field of staying and expecting.
note.cn: wait 与日耳曼「警觉」词族及「时间」义场相邻：形近组共享词根，近义组共享「停留与期待」义场。

entries.definition: to look at steadily, or to guard; a timepiece
entries.definitionCN: 观看、看守、手表；与 wait 同出日耳曼「醒着」词族

entries.definition: to stop sleeping, or to rouse someone
entries.definitionCN: 醒来、唤醒；与 wait 同族，本义即「醒着」

entries.definition: a man who serves food at tables
entries.definitionCN: 服务员；由 wait 加施动者后缀构成

entries.definition: the narrow middle part of the body
entries.definitionCN: 腰；与 wait 发音完全相同、仅拼写不同，词源不同，易混

entries.definition: how heavy something is
entries.definitionCN: 重量；与 wait 同音异拼，词源不同，是经典易混词

entries.definition: to believe something will come or happen
entries.definitionCN: 期待、预期；重在心里的预计，wait 重在停留本身

entries.definition: to stay longer than necessary, often unwilling to leave
entries.definitionCN: 徘徊、逗留；重在迟迟不走，wait 重在等某事

entries.definition: to stop briefly before continuing
entries.definitionCN: 暂停；短暂停顿，wait 可长可短

entries.definition: to make late, or postpone
entries.definitionCN: 延误、推迟；常含被动或造成的意味

entries.definition: to look forward to or act in advance of
entries.definitionCN: 预期、提前应对；正式用词

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the watchful Germanic family of wake, watch, and wait.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，全部来自 wake、watch、wait 共有的日耳曼「警觉」词族。

normal.en: the root means to stay awake watching; wait is watching without moving.
normal.cn: 词根意为醒着守候；wait 就是不动地注视。

normal.en: watch and wait are cousins: one guards with eyes, one stands still.
normal.cn: watch 与 wait 是表亲：一个用眼看守，一个站立不动。

normal.en: wake keeps the original sense: staying awake to wait.
normal.cn: wake 保留本义：醒着才等得到。

normal.en: wait tables shows the old service sense: watching for guests' needs.
normal.cn: wait tables 保留古老的服务义：留意客人所需。

normal.en: waist and weight sound the same as wait, but their letters differ.
normal.cn: waist 与 weight 与 wait 同音，但拼写不同，注意区分。

abstract.en: A figure on a bench facing the door, eyes open, feet still.
abstract.cn: 长椅上的人面朝门口，睁着眼，脚不动。

abstract.en: A kettle rising slowly to its whistle while you stand beside it.
abstract.cn: 水壶缓缓升温至鸣笛，而你站在旁边不动。

abstract.en: Time walks past you in the corridor; you stay and watch it go.
abstract.cn: 时间从走廊经过你身边，你留在原地看它走。

examples.en: The doctor asked us to wait outside for a few minutes.
examples.cn: 医生请我们在外面等几分钟。

examples.en: A letter was waiting on the table when she got home.
examples.cn: 她到家时，桌上正放着一封等她拆开的信。

examples.en: Investors chose to wait and see before moving their money.
examples.cn: 投资者选择先观望，再动用资金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂的」——等菜的时候喊「喂，点的呢？」一直等着上菜。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自日耳曼语「醒着守候」一族。

root: 日耳曼语词根 *waht-（醒着、警觉）→ 古北方法语 waitier（注视、看守）→ 中古英语 waiten（守望→等候）。与 wake（醒来）、watch（看守）同族，核心是「保持清醒的注视」。英语借自法语再回流日耳曼语义，是法语转手的日耳曼词。

sensesIntro.en: From watchful stillness outward: staying, being ready, the time spent, serving at table, and holding back.
sensesIntro.cn: 从警觉的静候向外铺开：停留、备好待命、等待的时间、伺候进餐，最后到按住不动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes awake, body still, holding a place for what is coming
core.cn: 核心意象：眼醒着，身不动，为将至之事守住位置

branches.en: The root sense: staying until the watched thing comes
branches.cn: 根本义：留驻到所盼之事到来

branches.en: Watchfulness turned service: readiness and attending
branches.cn: 守候化为服务：待命与照应

branches.en: The stillness itself, named and counted in time
branches.cn: 静候本身被命名、以时间计量

branches.en: Holding back one's own hand while hoping
branches.cn: 怀着希望按住自己的手

branches.en: Patience is waiting with the eyes open
branches.cn: 耐心就是睁着眼的等待

intro.en: The Germanic watch-root gathers wake, watch, and wait, and pairs with agent and service suffixes.
intro.cn: 日耳曼「警觉」词根聚起 wake、watch、wait 三词，并与施动、服务类后缀组合。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic; French waitier carried the old root back into English.
latinIntro.cn: 此词族属日耳曼来源；法语 waitier 把这一古老词根又送回英语。

items.exampleCN: watchful 与 waiting 同族的形容词

derivatives.zh: 服务员，由 wait 加施动者后缀构成
女服务员，由 waiter 加阴性后缀构成
等候，由 a- 加 wait 构成的及物动词

definition_zh: 醒来；唤醒；弄醒；觉醒；（船的）尾流；守灵
definition_en: to stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping; the track a boat leaves on water
core_image: 从黑暗的水面浮上来：眼睛睁开，世界的声音一起涌进来
scene: 清晨六点，闹钟在床头柜上震动。The smell of coffee was enough to wake him before the alarm rang.
sceneCN: 这里 wake 是「唤醒」（第 2 个义项：使某人停止睡眠）；句意是咖啡的香气足以让他在闹钟响之前醒来。

pos.zh: 动词：醒来；唤醒；弄醒；觉醒
名词：（船的）尾流；航迹；守灵

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「醒着的」，由 a- 加本词构成
动词，义为「唤醒、觉醒」，由 a- 加本词构成，偏书面
动词，义为「唤醒」，由本词加 -en 构成，偏正式
形容词，义为「醒着时的」，如 waking hours

senses.title: To stop sleeping
senses.titleCN: 醒来：停止睡眠
senses.definition: to stop being asleep and become conscious
senses.definitionCN: 停止睡眠，恢复意识
senses.example: She woke to the sound of birds outside the window.
senses.exampleCN: 她伴着窗外鸟鸣声醒来。
senses.why: The root means to be watchful; leaving sleep is returning to the watchful state.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义为警觉、醒着；离开睡眠就是回到警觉状态。

senses.title: To rouse someone from sleep
senses.titleCN: 唤醒：使某人停止睡眠
senses.definition: to make a person or animal stop sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 使人或动物停止睡眠
senses.example: The smell of coffee was enough to wake him before the alarm rang.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡的香气足以让他在闹钟响之前醒来。
senses.why: Watching over someone who sleeps, you may rouse them; the watchful hand wakes.
senses.whyCN: 守着睡着的人，便可能唤醒他，警觉之手使人转醒。

senses.title: To become aware or active
senses.titleCN: 觉醒：意识或活动被激发
senses.definition: to become alert, aware, or stirred into life, often in extended use
senses.definitionCN: 变得警觉、意识到或被激发出活力，常用于引申义
senses.example: The city wakes slowly on Sunday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 星期日的清晨，这座城市缓缓苏醒。
senses.why: What sleeps metaphorically can wake: towns, feelings, and nations stir alive.
senses.whyCN: 隐喻中沉睡之物亦可苏醒：城市、情感与民族纷纷焕发生机。

senses.title: The track behind a boat
senses.titleCN: 尾流：船后在水面留下的轨迹
senses.definition: the moving line or wave pattern left on water by a passing ship
senses.definitionCN: 船只驶过后在水面留下的波纹与轨迹
senses.example: The swimmers stayed clear of the ferry's wake.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳者们避开渡轮的尾流。
senses.why: A different line of development names the water's track behind the moving ship.
senses.whyCN: 此义另有词源脉络，指船只驶过时水面留下的痕迹。

senses.title: In the aftermath of something
senses.titleCN: 余波：在某事发生之后
senses.definition: used in the phrase in the wake of, meaning following closely after an event
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in the wake of，指紧随某事件之后
senses.example: Stores closed in the wake of the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，商店纷纷关门。
senses.why: A ship's wake trails behind it; events leave trails that follow them.
senses.whyCN: 船的尾流拖在船后，事件亦拖着尾随而来的余波。

senses.title: A vigil over the dead
senses.titleCN: 守灵：对逝者的通宵陪伴
senses.definition: a watch or vigil kept over a body before burial
senses.definitionCN: 下葬前对遗体彻夜的守候
senses.example: Friends kept a quiet wake through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 朋友们彻夜安静地守灵。
senses.why: The watchful root again: keeping vigil, eyes open through the night.
senses.whyCN: 又是「警觉」词根：守夜不眠，睁眼到天明。

intro.en: Wake is a native Germanic verb from the root meaning to be awake or watchful; the ship's wake comes by a different route from Old Norse.
intro.cn: wake 是日耳曼本族动词，词根意为醒着、警觉；「尾流」义则经古诺斯语以另一途径进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *waht- or *wak- means to be awake, lively, or watchful.
items.cn: 重构词根 *waht- 或 *wak- 意为醒着、有活力、警觉。

items.en: Wacan means to become awake; wacian means to be watchful; both survive as wake.
items.cn: 古英语 wacan 意为醒来，wacian 意为保持警觉，两者皆延续为 wake。

items.en: Waken covers both rousing oneself and rousing others, strong and weak forms alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 waken 兼指唤醒自己与他人，强弱变化形式并存。

items.en: The ship's wake enters via Old Norse vok, a hole or track in ice, later applied to water trails.
items.cn: 「尾流」义经古诺斯语 vok（冰上的洞或轨迹）进入，后用于指水面航迹。

items.en: The nautical sense settles as the visible track behind a moving vessel.
items.cn: 15 至 16 世纪，航海义定型，指船只驶过留下的可见轨迹。

items.en: Wake now spans waking up, waking others, wakes of ships, and wakes for the dead.
items.cn: 如今 wake 涵盖醒来、唤醒、船的尾流与逝者的守灵。

note.en: Wake sits at the center of its own Germanic family; look-alikes share the awake-root, near meanings share the field of rousing and vigil.
note.cn: wake 处于自身日耳曼词族的中心：形近组共享「醒」词根，近义组共享「唤醒与守夜」义场。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Germanic awake-family and the Norse water-track route.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自日耳曼「醒」词族与古诺斯语「水迹」一脉。

normal.en: the root means watchful; wake is the moment of becoming watchful again.
normal.cn: 词根意为警觉；wake 就是重新变得警觉的那一刻。

normal.en: awake, awaken, waken are all built on the same old verb.
normal.cn: awake、awaken、waken 都建立在同一个古老动词之上。

normal.en: woke and woken are the irregular past forms to memorize.
normal.cn: woke 与 woken 是需要记住的不规则过去式与过去分词。

normal.en: in the wake of borrows the ship's trail for events' aftermath.
normal.cn: in the wake of 借用船的尾流来比喻事件的余波。

normal.en: a wake for the dead keeps the oldest sense: eyes open all night.
normal.cn: 守灵保留最古老的义项：整夜睁眼。

abstract.en: A diver rising through dark water breaks into light and sound.
abstract.cn: 潜水者从黑暗的水中上浮，破入光与声。

abstract.en: Two white lines of water fold behind a boat, holding its memory for a while.
abstract.cn: 船后两道白色水痕缓缓收拢，替它保存一小段记忆。

abstract.en: A whole street lights window by window, as if one lamp woke the next.
abstract.cn: 整条街一扇窗一扇窗地亮起，仿佛一盏灯唤醒了下一盏。

examples.en: Don't wake the baby; she just fell asleep.
examples.cn: 别吵醒宝宝，她刚睡着。

examples.en: The scandal left a long wake across the industry.
examples.cn: 这桩丑闻在整个行业留下了长长的余波。

examples.en: He woke early and watched the sunrise from the balcony.
examples.cn: 他醒得很早，在阳台上看日出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂克」——早晨喊「喂，快克（刻）服睡意！」人就醒了。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自日耳曼语「醒着、警觉」。

root: 日耳曼语词根 *wak-（醒着、警觉）→ 古英语 wacan（醒来）、wacian（保持警觉）→ 现代英语 wake。「尾流」义经古诺斯语 vok（冰上轨迹）另途进入。同族词有 awake、awaken、waken、watch（看守）、wait（经法语转手的同族词）。核心是「保持清醒的注视」。

sensesIntro.en: From the opening eyes outward: waking, rousing others, stirring to life, the ship's trail, and the night watch.
sensesIntro.cn: 从睁开的眼睛向外铺开：醒来、唤醒他人、焕发生机、船的尾迹，最后到彻夜的守候。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the crossing line between sleep and watchfulness
core.cn: 核心意象：睡眠与警觉之间的那条交界线

branches.en: The root crossing: from sleep to watchful consciousness
branches.cn: 根本的跨越：从睡眠到警觉的意识

branches.en: The crossing done to another person
branches.cn: 替他人完成的跨越：唤醒

branches.en: The crossing in metaphor: cities and feelings come alive
branches.cn: 隐喻中的跨越：城市与情感焕发生机

branches.en: The Norse trail: water lines and the events that trail behind
branches.cn: 诺斯语的轨迹：水痕与尾随事件的余波

branches.en: Watchfulness kept through the night for the dead
branches.cn: 为逝者彻夜保持的警觉：守灵

intro.en: The Germanic awake-root builds a dense family with prefixes and the verb-ending -en.
intro.cn: 日耳曼「醒」词根借助前缀与动词后缀 -en 构成密集词族。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic; there is no Latin cognate inside English wake.
latinIntro.cn: 此词族属日耳曼来源，英语 wake 内部并无拉丁同族词。

definition_en: to move forward on foot at a regular pace, lifting and setting down each foot in turn
core_image: 双脚轮流落地：一步一步，把路踩在脚下
scene: 天刚亮，山路上已有薄雾。We walked along the river until the sun climbed over the hills.
sceneCN: 这里 walk 是「步行」（第 1 个义项：双脚轮流前进）；句意是我们沿河步行，直到太阳爬上山头。

senses.title: To move on foot
senses.titleCN: 步行：双脚轮流前进
senses.definition: to move forward at a regular pace by lifting and setting down each foot in turn
senses.definitionCN: 以平稳的速度前进，双脚轮流抬起落下
senses.example: We walked along the river until the sun climbed over the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿河步行，直到太阳爬上山头。
senses.why: Old English wealcan meant to roll or turn over; feet turning over the ground became walking.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wealcan 意为滚动、翻转；双脚在地面上轮流翻转行进，便成了步行。

senses.title: To go somewhere with someone
senses.titleCN: 陪走：陪伴某人步行前往
senses.definition: to go on foot with someone, or to make a dog or child move on foot
senses.definitionCN: 陪某人步行前往，或带狗、孩子等步行
senses.example: He walked her home after the evening class.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间课程结束后，他陪她走回家。
senses.why: Your steps carry another along; walking extends from yourself to those you escort.
senses.whyCN: 你的脚步把他人一并带上，步行之义从自身延伸到所陪伴的对象。

senses.title: To move or travel in a stated way
senses.titleCN: 行走的状态：以特定方式移动
senses.definition: to move on foot in the manner mentioned, or to travel in a stated way
senses.definitionCN: 以所描述的方式步行或移动
senses.example: She walked confidently into the interview room.
senses.exampleCN: 她步履从容地走进面试间。
senses.why: The manner of the steps reveals the person; walking carries style inside it.
senses.whyCN: 脚步的方式透露其人，行走之中自带姿态。

senses.title: A journey made on foot
senses.titleCN: 步行之旅：一段步行的路程
senses.definition: a journey or distance covered on foot; a route for walking
senses.definitionCN: 步行完成的路程，或供步行的路线
senses.example: The coastal walk takes about three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这条海滨步道大约要走三个小时。
senses.why: The act of walking hardens into the path itself and the trip along it.
senses.whyCN: 步行这一行为凝固成路径本身与沿路径的行程。

senses.title: A way of stepping; manner
senses.titleCN: 步态：走路的姿态与风度
senses.definition: the manner or style of a person's walking; a slow pace like a walk
senses.definitionCN: 一个人走路的方式、姿态，或如散步般的缓慢速度
senses.example: The old sailor still had a rolling walk.
senses.exampleCN: 老水手走路仍带着摇晃的步态。
senses.why: Steps repeated long enough become a signature; the gait is the walk remembered.
senses.whyCN: 脚步重复久了便成印记，步态就是被记住的行走方式。

senses.title: A social class or occupation
senses.titleCN: 阶层：walk of life 中的行业与身份
senses.definition: in the phrase walk of life, a person's occupation, class, or position in society
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 walk of life，指职业、阶层或社会身份
senses.example: Visitors from every walk of life come to the fair.
senses.exampleCN: 各行各业的人都来逛这个集市。
senses.why: Where you walk daily is where you live and work; the path stands for the life.
senses.whyCN: 日常行走之处即生活与劳作之处，路径便成了人生的代称。

intro.en: Walk is a native Germanic word from Old English wealcan, to roll, turn, or move about, whose sense narrowed to moving on foot.
intro.cn: walk 是日耳曼本族词，源自古英语 wealcan（滚动、翻转、四处移动），词义后来收窄为步行。

items.en: The reconstructed root *walk- or *welk- means to roll, turn, or wind one's way along.
items.cn: 重构词根 *walk- 或 *welk- 意为滚动、翻转、蜿蜒前行。

items.en: Wealcan means to roll, toss, or travel about; walking is one motion among many.
items.cn: 古英语 wealcan 意为滚动、颠簸、四处行走，步行只是诸多移动方式之一。

items.en: Walken narrows to mean traveling on foot, displacing older go for ordinary walking.
items.cn: 中古英语 walken 词义收窄为徒步前行，在「日常步行」上取代了更早的 go。

items.en: The sense of a deliberate, unhurried pace develops, a pace slower than running.
items.cn: 13 至 14 世纪，从容不迫的步速之义形成，慢于奔跑。

items.en: The noun grows: a walk becomes an outing, a path, and even a place for strolling.
items.cn: 15 至 16 世纪名词义生长：walk 成为出游、路径乃至散步场所。

items.en: Walk now spans steps, escorts, dog walks, gait, and walks of life.
items.cn: 如今 walk 涵盖步行、陪走、遛狗、步态与各行各业。

note.en: Walk stands beside its Germanic rolling family and the foot-travel word-field; look-alikes share the root, near meanings share the field of moving on foot.
note.cn: walk 与日耳曼「滚动」词族及「徒步」义场相邻：形近组共享词根，近义组共享步行义场。

entries.definitionCN: 烛芯；词形相近，词源完全不同

entries.definition: to walk in a slow, relaxed way
entries.definitionCN: 漫步、闲逛；强调轻松缓慢

entries.definition: to walk with long, confident steps
entries.definitionCN: 大步走；强调步伐大而有劲

entries.definition: to walk around without a fixed purpose
entries.definitionCN: 游荡、漫游；强调没有固定方向

entries.definition: to walk with regular steps, especially back and forth
entries.definitionCN: 踱步；强调有规律地来回走

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Germanic rolling root and the walking word-family.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自日耳曼「滚动」词根及步行词族。

normal.en: the old root meant to roll; feet roll over the ground step by step.
normal.cn: 古老词根意为滚动；双脚在地面上一轮一轮前进。

normal.en: the letter l and c in old wealcan softened into the modern k sound.
normal.cn: 古词 wealcan 中的字母组合软化成现代的 k 音。

normal.en: walk the dog keeps the escort sense: your steps carry another.
normal.cn: walk the dog 保留「伴随」义：你的脚步带上另一个。

normal.en: walk of life turns the daily path into social class.
normal.cn: walk of life 把日常的路径变成社会身份。

normal.en: go for a walk is the everyday phrase for a gentle outing.
normal.cn: go for a walk 是日常散步的惯用说法。

abstract.en: Two wheels of feet turning slowly over the earth, printing one mark after another.
abstract.cn: 双脚如两只轮子缓缓碾过大地，留下一枚又一枚印迹。

abstract.en: A path grows under your soles: walk far enough and the way becomes yours.
abstract.cn: 路在脚底生长：走得够远，这条路便属于你。

abstract.en: Slow steps keep company better than fast ones; escorting is walking beside.
abstract.cn: 慢步比快步更宜同行；陪伴就是走在旁边。

examples.en: It takes ten minutes to walk from the station to the office.
examples.cn: 从车站走到办公室需要十分钟。

examples.en: They walked the whole beach at sunset, talking quietly.
examples.cn: 日落时分他们沿着海滩走了一整段，轻声交谈。

examples.en: The new park has shaded walks along both sides of the lake.
examples.cn: 新公园的湖的两侧都有林荫步道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我靠」——走得太久，停下来喊一声「我靠，累！」才想起 walk 就是走。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自古英语 wealcan（滚动前行）。

root: 日耳曼语词根 *welk-（滚动、翻转）→ 古英语 wealcan（滚动、四处行走）→ 中古英语 walken（收窄为步行）。本族词，无拉丁同源。同族复合法众多：walkway、jaywalk、catwalk、boardwalk 等，核心意象是「轮流翻动、蜿蜒前行」。

sensesIntro.en: From the rolling steps outward: moving on foot, escorting others, the manner of movement, the path itself, and the life you walk through.
sensesIntro.cn: 从滚动的脚步向外铺开：徒步行进、陪伴同行、移动的姿态、路径本身，最后到所走过的人生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet rolling over the ground, one step after another
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚在地面轮流翻动，一步一步向前

branches.en: The root motion: travel on foot at a steady pace
branches.cn: 根本动作：以平稳速度徒步前行

branches.en: Steps shared: walking with and for another
branches.cn: 共享的脚步：陪伴他人行走

branches.en: The style inside the steps: manner and gait
branches.cn: 脚步里的风格：方式与步态

branches.en: The act frozen into paths and routes
branches.cn: 行为凝固成路径与路线

branches.en: Where you walk daily becomes who you are
branches.cn: 日常行走之处，便是你之所是

intro.cn: 日耳曼 walk 词根主要出现在复合词中，与「路、板、鸟」等成分结合。

definition_zh: 墙；墙壁；围墙；屏障；隔阂
definition_en: a vertical structure that divides or surrounds an area, or anything that acts like such a barrier
core_image: 一面立起来的墙：挡住风、挡住视线，也挡住人心
scene: 院子里，爷爷砌砖的动作稳而有节奏。The children drew a small door on the garden wall with chalk.
sceneCN: 这里 wall 是「墙」（第 1 个义项：砌起的直立结构）；句意是孩子们用粉笔在院墙上画了一扇小门。

pos.zh: 名词：墙；围墙；屏障；隔阂
动词：用墙围住；以墙隔开

senses.title: A vertical structure of a building
senses.titleCN: 墙：建筑物的直立墙体
senses.definition: one of the upright sides of a building or room, made of brick, stone, or wood
senses.definitionCN: 建筑或房间的直立边壁，由砖、石、木等构成
senses.example: The children drew a small door on the garden wall with chalk.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用粉笔在院墙上画了一扇小门。
senses.why: Latin vallum means a rampart; the defense line becomes the everyday wall.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vallum 意为壁垒；防线演变为日常的墙体。

senses.title: A fence around a place
senses.titleCN: 围墙：环绕一地的防护结构
senses.definition: a structure built around a city, garden, or field to enclose or protect it
senses.definitionCN: 围绕城市、花园或田地而建、用于围护的结构
senses.example: The old town still keeps its medieval walls.
senses.exampleCN: 老城至今仍保留着中世纪的城墙。
senses.why: The rampart sense stays closest to the root: walls first shielded whole towns.
senses.whyCN: 壁垒之义最贴近词源：墙最初守护的是整座城。

senses.title: Anything that blocks or separates
senses.titleCN: 屏障：起阻挡或分隔作用之物
senses.definition: anything that acts as a physical or mental barrier
senses.definitionCN: 起物理或心理阻挡作用的任何事物
senses.example: The wall of sound made conversation impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 声浪如墙，让人无法交谈。
senses.why: What stands between you and the other side works like masonry, whatever it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 凡隔在你与另一侧之间的东西，都如砖石之墙起作用，无论它由什么构成。

senses.title: Emotional distance between people
senses.titleCN: 隔阂：人与人之间的心理之墙
senses.definition: a feeling of separation or lack of communication between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间的疏离感或沟通障碍
senses.example: After the quarrel there was a wall of silence between them.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后，沉默如墙横在他们之间。
senses.why: The barrier moves inward: instead of stone, silence and pride stand between.
senses.whyCN: 屏障移入内心：立于两人之间的不再是石头，而是沉默与自尊。

senses.title: A limit you cannot pass
senses.titleCN: 极限：无法越过的瓶颈
senses.definition: a point beyond which progress becomes impossible
senses.definitionCN: 进展无法再推进的临界点
senses.example: By midnight the exhausted runners hit the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 到午夜时，精疲力竭的选手们撞上了极限之墙。
senses.why: Running forward, you meet something immovable; progress stops like a body against stone.
senses.whyCN: 向前奔跑却撞上不可撼动之物，前进如身体撞上石壁般停止。

intro.en: Wall descends from Latin vallum, a rampart of stakes or earth, through Germanic and Norman borrowing into English.
intro.cn: wall 上溯至拉丁语 vallum（木栅或土筑的壁垒），经日耳曼诸语与诺曼借用进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *wel- means to turn or roll; stakes turned into a fence may underlie the rampart word.
items.cn: 重构词根 *wel- 意为转动、环绕；「围栏」义或由木桩绕转成篱而来。

items.en: Vallum means a rampart or line of stakes defending a camp or town.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vallum 意为壁垒，即保卫营地或城镇的木栅防线。

items.en: Latin vallum was borrowed very early into Germanic languages as *wal-, a defensive wall.
items.cn: vallum 很早便被借入日耳曼诸语作 *wal-，指防御性围墙。

items.en: Weall means a wall, rampart, or dam; both defense and enclosure senses exist.
items.cn: 古英语 weall 意为墙、壁垒、堤坝，防御与围合两义并存。

items.en: The everyday building sense broadens while the defensive sense persists in city walls.
items.cn: 中古时期，日常建筑义扩展，防御义则保留在「城墙」中。

items.en: Wall now covers masonry, barriers, bottlenecks, and emotional distance alike.
items.cn: 如今 wall 涵盖砖石之墙、屏障、瓶颈与心理隔阂。

note.en: Wall belongs to the Latin rampart family and the barrier word-field; look-alikes share spelling, near meanings share the field of blocking and enclosing.
note.cn: wall 属拉丁「壁垒」词族及「阻隔」义场：形近组共享拼形，近义组共享阻挡与围合义场。

entries.definitionCN: 壁纸；由 wall 加 paper 构成

entries.definitionCN: 凸纹、船侧板条；与 wall 拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the very large sea mammal
entries.definitionCN: 鲸；与 wall 一字母之差，词源无关，易混

entries.definition: a broad bank or wall for defense
entries.definitionCN: 壁垒、防御土墙；法语词源，与 wall 义场相邻但来源不同

entries.definition: a structure of posts and rails dividing land
entries.definitionCN: 栅栏、篱笆；透空且较轻的围护

entries.definition: a thing that prevents passage or progress
entries.definitionCN: 障碍、屏障；泛指一切阻挡之物

entries.definition: an inner dividing wall or screen
entries.definitionCN: 隔断、隔墙；强调内部分隔

entries.definition: a row of bushes forming a boundary
entries.definitionCN: 树篱；植物构成的围界

entries.definition: to separate, or the line of separation itself
entries.definitionCN: 分隔、分界；与墙的隔合义相对的是动作与界线

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Latin rampart root vallum and its English descendants.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自拉丁壁垒词根 vallum 及其英语后裔。

normal.en: vallum means rampart; a wall was first a line of defense.
normal.cn: vallum 意为壁垒；wall 最初就是一道防线。

normal.en: the Latin v softened to w in Germanic borrowing: vallum to weall to wall.
normal.cn: 拉丁 v 在日耳曼借用中软化为 w：vallum 变 weall 再变 wall。

normal.en: city walls keeps the oldest defensive sense alive.
normal.cn: city walls（城墙）保留着最古老的防御义。

normal.en: hit the wall borrows the stone barrier for exhaustion.
normal.cn: hit the wall 借石墙比喻撞上极限。

normal.en: walls have ears warns that barriers do not stop sound.
normal.cn: walls have ears（隔墙有耳）提醒我们墙挡不住声音。

abstract.en: Two hands lay stone upon stone until nothing on the other side can be seen.
abstract.cn: 双手把石头一层层垒起，直到另一侧的一切都看不见。

abstract.en: Silence stands in a doorway like a brick wall nobody built.
abstract.cn: 沉默立在门口，像一堵无人砌起的砖墙。

abstract.en: At dawn a chalk door appears on the wall: children still believe in ways through.
abstract.cn: 清晨墙上出现一扇粉笔画的门：孩子们仍相信总有穿墙之路。

examples.en: They built a low stone wall around the vegetable garden.
examples.cn: 他们在菜园四周砌了一道矮石墙。

examples.en: Months of training collapsed when he suddenly hit a wall.
examples.cn: 数月的训练在他突然撞上瓶颈时功亏一篑。

examples.en: Hang the picture on the wall opposite the window.
examples.cn: 把画挂在窗户对面那面墙上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我堵」——「我堵在这儿，谁也别想过去！」墙的作用就是堵。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自拉丁 vallum（壁垒）。

root: 拉丁语 vallum（木栅壁垒，或源自 *wel-「环绕转动」）→ 早期借入日耳曼诸语作 *wal- → 古英语 weall（墙、壁垒、堤坝）→ 现代英语 wall。这条「拉丁→日耳曼→英语」的借用路径十分古老，同源词还有 古诺斯语 völlr（原野）等说法，存有争议。

sensesIntro.en: From the rampart outward: building walls, town walls, barriers of any kind, silence between people, and the limits of body and effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 从壁垒向外铺开：建筑之墙、城镇之墙、各式屏障、人际沉默，最后到身体与努力的极限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of defense raised between here and there
core.cn: 核心意象：在此与彼之间竖起的一道防线

branches.en: The everyday wall: upright masonry of rooms and houses
branches.cn: 日常之墙：房屋与房间的直立壁体

branches.en: The root sense: town and garden enclosures for defense
branches.cn: 词源本义：护城的城墙与围园之墙

branches.en: Whatever blocks you: sound, exhaustion, and limits
branches.cn: 一切阻挡之物：声浪、疲惫与极限

branches.en: The wall inside hearts: silence between people
branches.cn: 人心内的墙：人与人之间的沉默

branches.en: Barriers do not only stop feet; they stop words too
branches.cn: 屏障不止挡住脚步，也挡住言语

intro.en: The wall-root lives mostly in compounds, joining with paper, sockets, streets, and flowers.
intro.cn: wall 词根主要活在复合词中，与「纸、插座、街、花」等成分结合。

latinIntro.en: Latin vallum has no direct Latin derivatives in English besides wall itself.
latinIntro.cn: 除 wall 本身外，拉丁 vallum 在英语中没有其他直接派生。

items.meaningCN: 墙角花；舞会中羞怯的人

definition_zh: 漫游；徘徊；闲逛；走神；偏离（正题、路线）
definition_en: to walk around slowly without a clear purpose or direction, or to let thoughts drift
core_image: 没有目的地的脚步：风往哪吹，人就往哪走
scene: 傍晚的老城巷子，灯光一盏盏亮起。After dinner she wandered through the old streets without any plan.
sceneCN: 这里 wander 是「闲逛」（第 1 个义项：无目的地漫游）；句意是晚饭后她在老街间随意漫步，没有既定安排。

pos.zh: 动词：漫游；徘徊；闲逛；走神；偏离
名词：漫游；徘徊

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「漫游者、流浪者」，由动词加施动者后缀构成
形容词，义为「漫游的、蜿蜒的」，由现在分词转作定语
名词，义为「漫游欲、旅行癖」，由 wander 加德语 Lust（欲望）构成

senses.title: To walk without purpose
senses.titleCN: 闲逛：没有目的地的步行
senses.definition: to walk around slowly and aimlessly, for pleasure or from restlessness
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而随意地四处走动，或为消遣，或因躁动
senses.example: After dinner she wandered through the old streets without any plan.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她在老街间随意漫步，没有既定安排。
senses.why: Middle English wandren meant to stray from the path; steps without a goal keep straying.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语 wandren 意为偏离路径；没有目标的脚步一直在「偏」。

senses.title: To move off course
senses.titleCN: 偏离：离开应有的路线
senses.definition: to move away from a route, place, or proper position
senses.definitionCN: 离开既定路线、地点或应有的位置
senses.example: The sheep wandered from the flock and got lost.
senses.exampleCN: 那只羊离了羊群，走丢了。
senses.why: Straying is the core image: the path exists, but feet choose elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 「走偏」是核心意象：路明明在那里，脚却选择了别处。

senses.title: To lose concentration
senses.titleCN: 走神：思绪失去焦点
senses.definition: to let thoughts drift away from the matter at hand
senses.definitionCN: 让思绪从眼前之事漂移开去
senses.example: His mind wandered during the long lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的讲座中，他的思绪走神了。
senses.why: The mind has paths too; attention that strays is attention that wanders.
senses.whyCN: 思绪也有路径，注意力一「走偏」，便是走神。

senses.title: To drift through places over time
senses.titleCN: 漂泊：长时段、长距离的流转
senses.definition: to travel from place to place over a long period without a fixed home
senses.definitionCN: 长时期辗转各地，没有固定的居所
senses.example: He wandered the world for a decade before settling down.
senses.exampleCN: 他漂泊了十年才安定下来。
senses.why: One stray after another, stretched over years, becomes a life without a fixed path.
senses.whyCN: 一次次的偏离延伸成年月，便成了没有固定路径的人生。

senses.title: A curve or slow stretch
senses.titleCN: 蜿蜒：路径或话语的曲折
senses.definition: of a path, river, or talk, to proceed in a slow, curving, indirect way
senses.definitionCN: 指小路、河流或谈话缓慢、弯曲、迂回地进行
senses.example: The river wanders across the plain in slow bends.
senses.exampleCN: 河流在大平原上蜿蜒缓行。
senses.why: A path that never goes straight keeps straying from the direct line.
senses.whyCN: 从不走直线的路径，便是在不断偏离直线。

intro.en: Wander comes from Old English wandrian, to move about aimlessly, of Germanic origin, possibly related to wend and wind.
intro.cn: wander 源自古英语 wandrian（无目的地走动），属日耳曼来源，一般认为可能与 wend（转向）和 wind（蜿蜒）相关。

items.en: The reconstructed root behind wandrian involves turning and winding movement; its wider links are generally believed rather than proven.
items.cn: wandrian 背后的重构词根涉及转弯与蜿蜒的移动；其更宽泛的同源联系属于普遍推定。

items.en: Wandrian means to wander, journey about, or stray from the path.
items.cn: 古英语 wandrian 意为游荡、四处行走、偏离路径。

items.en: Wandren keeps the senses of aimless motion and straying from the right way.
items.cn: 中古英语 wandren 保留「无目的移动」与「偏离正路」两义。

items.en: The sense extends to wandering minds, wandering rivers, and wandering peoples.
items.cn: 15 至 16 世纪，词义扩展到走神的思绪、蜿蜒的河流与迁徙的民族。

items.en: German Wanderlust forms inside the same family, borrowed back into English for the love of roaming.
items.cn: 19 世纪，德语 Wanderlust 在同一词族内构成，又被英语借回，指对漫游的热爱。

items.en: Wander now covers feet, rivers, minds, and planets, from wandering off to wandering stars.
items.cn: 如今 wander 涵盖脚步、河流、思绪与行星，从走散到「游星」皆有此词。

note.en: Wander stands at the center of its Germanic straying family; look-alikes share the root and spelling traps, near meanings share the field of aimless motion.
note.cn: wander 处于日耳曼「游荡」词族中心：形近组共享词根与拼写陷阱，近义组共享「无目的移动」义场。

entries.definition: a person who wanders, a rover
entries.definitionCN: 漫游者；由 wander 加施动者后缀构成

entries.definition: a strong desire to travel and roam
entries.definitionCN: 旅行癖；由 wander 加德语 Lust 构成

entries.definition: to feel curiosity or doubt; a marvel
entries.definitionCN: 好奇、疑惑、奇迹；与 wander 仅一字母之差，词源不同，是最经典的易混词

entries.definition: to go in a particular direction, slowly
entries.definitionCN: 缓缓前行；一般认为与 wander 同源相关

entries.definition: to follow a winding course
entries.definitionCN: 迂回行进；源自小亚细亚一条曲折河流的名字，词源与 wander 不同

entries.definition: to walk for pleasure, or to talk at length without focus
entries.definitionCN: 漫步、闲谈离题；兼指脚与嘴的漫游

entries.definition: to move about widely over an area
entries.definitionCN: 漫游、徜徉；强调范围广

entries.definition: to walk in a slow, relaxed way
entries.definitionCN: 散步、闲逛；强调轻松，不强调无方向

entries.definition: to move slowly without direction, carried by forces
entries.definitionCN: 漂移；多用于水、雾、人群与思绪

entries.definition: to move away from the group or the correct path
entries.definitionCN: 走失、偏离；强调离开应有的位置

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Germanic straying family and its famous spelling twin.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自日耳曼「游荡」词族及其著名的拼写孪生词。

normal.en: the root means to stray from the path; wandering is one long stray.
normal.cn: 词根意为偏离路径；wandering 就是一次长长的偏离。

normal.en: wander has an a, wonder has an o: feet wander, minds wonder.
normal.cn: wander 有 a，wonder 有 o：脚会 wander（游荡），心会 wonder（好奇）。

normal.en: wanderlust is German-built: wander plus Lust, desire to roam.
normal.cn: wanderlust 是德语造词：wander 加 Lust（欲望），即漫游之欲。

normal.en: wander off is the phrase for straying away or daydreaming.
normal.cn: wander off 既指走散，也指走神。

normal.en: wandering stars was an old name for planets that drift across the sky.
normal.cn: wandering stars（游星）是古人对行星的称呼，因其漂移于星空。

abstract.en: A paper boat left on a stream goes where the current likes.
abstract.cn: 放在溪流上的纸船，去往水流喜欢去的地方。

abstract.en: A path drawn in pencil, curved and erased and curved again.
abstract.cn: 一条用铅笔画出的路径，弯了又擦，擦了又弯。

abstract.en: In class your eyes stay on the board while your feet walk invisible roads.
abstract.cn: 课堂上眼睛盯着黑板，脚却在走看不见的路。

examples.en: We wandered around the market all morning, tasting whatever looked good.
examples.cn: 整个上午我们在集市里闲逛，见到想吃的就尝一口。

examples.en: The conversation wandered from weather to old school days.
examples.cn: 谈话从天气漫游到旧日校园。

examples.en: A stray cat wandered into the yard and stayed for years.
examples.cn: 一只流浪猫游荡进了院子，一住就是好几年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「 wander ≈ 万得」——「万得自在」，想去哪就去哪，千般路线任你选。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自古英语 wandrian（游荡）。

root: 日耳曼语词根（一般认为与 *wend-「转向」相关）→ 古英语 wandrian（无目的地游荡、偏离路径）→ 中古英语 wandren → 现代英语 wander。与 wend（前行）可能同源；注意与 wonder（好奇，源自古英语 wundor）词源完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: From straying steps outward: aimless walking, losing the route, drifting minds, years of roaming, and the slow curves of rivers and talk.
sensesIntro.cn: 从偏离的脚步向外铺开：漫无目的的走、迷路的偏、走神的心、经年的漂泊，最后到河流与谈话的蜿蜒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steps that keep choosing anywhere but the straight line
core.cn: 核心意象：脚步总在选择直线以外的任何方向

branches.en: The root pleasure: walking with nowhere to be
branches.cn: 根本的乐趣：无处可去之地的闲步

branches.en: The stray and the curve: off route, winding on
branches.cn: 偏离与蜿蜒：离了路线，弯着前行

branches.en: The mind's own wandering: attention off its path
branches.cn: 思绪的游荡：注意力偏离其路径

branches.en: Strays stretched over years become a roving life
branches.cn: 偏离延伸成年月，便成漂泊人生

branches.en: Homeless motion, from evening stroll to lifetime journey
branches.cn: 无居所的移动，从傍晚闲逛到一生行旅

intro.en: The Germanic straying root builds mostly compounds and agent nouns in modern English.
intro.cn: 日耳曼「游荡」词根在现代英语中主要构成复合词与施动名词。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic; Latin has no direct cognate in the wander-family.
latinIntro.cn: 此词族属日耳曼来源，wander 词族中没有直接的拉丁同源词。

definition_zh: 想要；希望；需要；缺乏；贫乏
definition_en: to wish to have or do something, or to lack something needed

scene: 橱窗前，孩子把鼻尖贴上了玻璃。The boy pressed his nose to the window and said he wanted that red bicycle.

pos.zh: 动词：想要；希望；需要；缺乏
名词：缺乏；需要；想要的东西

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「被需要的；被通缉的」，由过去分词转作定语

senses.title: To wish to have or do
senses.titleCN: 想要：希望拥有或去做
senses.definition: to feel a wish or desire for something, or to do something
senses.definitionCN: 对某物或某事心怀愿望与渴求
senses.example: The boy pressed his nose to the window and said he wanted that red bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩把鼻尖贴在橱窗上说，他想要那辆红色自行车。
senses.why: Old Norse vanta meant to lack; what you lack, you reach for, and reaching becomes wanting.
senses.whyCN: 古诺斯语 vanta 意为缺乏；缺了便伸手去够，伸手便成了想要。

senses.title: To need or require
senses.titleCN: 需要：为了某目的而要求
senses.definition: to need something, or to require someone to do something
senses.definitionCN: 需要某物，或要求某人做某事
senses.example: This plant wants full sunlight and weekly watering.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物需要全日照和每周浇水。
senses.why: Lack and need are the same root: what is missing is what is required.
senses.whyCN: 缺乏与需要本是同一根源：缺什么，就要求什么。

senses.title: To lack
senses.titleCN: 缺乏：应有而无
senses.definition: to not have something that is needed or expected
senses.definitionCN: 没有本该拥有的必需之物
senses.example: The old bridge wants repairs before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧桥在入冬前需要整修，眼下正缺修缮。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives here: want was first of all absence.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项在此存留：want 首先是一种「没有」。

senses.title: Poverty and hardship
senses.titleCN: 贫困：生活的匮乏
senses.definition: the state of not having enough money or the basic things of life
senses.definitionCN: 缺钱少物、生计艰难的状态
senses.example: The family knew real want during those winters.
senses.exampleCN: 那些冬天，这家人尝过真正的匮乏。
senses.why: Personal lack widened to whole households; absence of things became absence of living.
senses.whyCN: 个体的缺乏扩及整个家庭，物品之缺成了生计之缺。

senses.title: A thing wished for; desires
senses.titleCN: 想要的东西：心愿与需求
senses.definition: something desired, or desires and needs considered together
senses.definitionCN: 所希望之物，或泛指种种心愿与需求
senses.example: We listed our wants and needs before moving house.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家前我们列出了想要与必需的清单。
senses.why: Each lack names itself as a thing; wants become countable nouns.
senses.whyCN: 每一份缺失都把自己变成一件东西，want 于是成了可数的名词。

senses.title: Wanted by authority
senses.titleCN: 被通缉的：被官方所「需要」
senses.definition: used of a person whom the police or authorities are seeking
senses.definitionCN: 指警方或当局正在寻找的人
senses.example: The notice showed the face of a wanted man.
senses.exampleCN: 布告上贴着一名被通缉者的面孔。
senses.why: To be required by power is to be wanted; need turns into pursuit.
senses.whyCN: 被权力所需要即被「想要」，需要转为追索。

intro.en: Want descends from Old Norse vanta, to lack, borrowed into Middle English; its deeper root is generally believed Germanic rather than Latin.
intro.cn: want 上溯至古诺斯语 vanta（缺乏），借入中古英语；其更深的词根一般认为属日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.en: A reconstructed root *wan- or *wanat- meaning lack or insufficiency is generally proposed for the family.
items.cn: 一般认为该词族可重构词根 *wan- 或 *wanat-，意为缺乏、不足。

items.en: Vanta means to lack, to be in need of.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 vanta 意为缺乏、需要。

items.en: Related forms such as wan- (lacking) appear, as in wanhus, a house lacking goods; the verb itself arrives with Norse influence.
items.cn: 相关形式如前缀 wan-（缺乏）已见于古英语，动词本体则随诺斯语影响传入。

items.en: Wanten means to lack or be short of; the sense of desire grows out of the lack.
items.cn: 中古英语 wanten 意为缺乏、短缺；「渴望」义由「缺」中生出。

items.en: The noun want names poverty and hardship, as in the phrase for want of.
items.cn: 16 至 18 世纪，名词 want 指贫困与匮乏，如短语 for want of。

items.en: Want now leads everyday speech for desire, from wanting tea to the wanted posters of crime pages.
items.cn: 如今 want 是日常表达愿望的首选词，从想喝杯茶到通缉令上的 wanted。

note.en: Want sits beside its Norse lack-family and the desire word-field; look-alikes share the root, near meanings share the field of wishing and needing.
note.cn: want 与诺斯语「缺乏」词族及「愿望」义场相邻：形近组共享词根，近义组共享「希望与需要」义场。

entries.definition: a strong feeling of wanting something
entries.definitionCN: 欲望、渴望；语气更强、更抽象

entries.definition: to require something necessary
entries.definitionCN: 需要；强调必要性，want 强调愿望

entries.definition: to hope for something unlikely or unattainable
entries.definitionCN: 但愿、希望；常指难以实现之事

entries.definition: to want something intensely
entries.definitionCN: 渴求；强调强烈到近乎身不由己

entries.definition: to not have enough of something
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏；与 want 最古老的义项直接对应

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Norse lack-root and the everyday desire-family.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自诺斯语「缺乏」词根与日常愿望词族。

normal.en: the old root means lack; wanting is a lack that reaches out.
normal.cn: 古老词根意为缺乏；wanting 是一种伸出手去的缺乏。

normal.en: for want of keeps the fossil sense: for lack of.
normal.cn: for want of 保存着化石义：即「因缺乏」。

normal.en: wanting as an adjective still means lacking or imperfect.
normal.cn: wanting 作形容词仍指欠缺、不完满。

normal.en: wan and want may share the pale, insufficient family.
normal.cn: wan（苍白）与 want 或同属「不足、失色」一族。

normal.en: wanted posters flip the sense: now the state wants you.
normal.cn: 通缉令上的 wanted 反转词义：这次是当局「想要」你。

abstract.en: A hand stretched through shop glass toward something bright and out of reach.
abstract.cn: 一只手穿过橱窗玻璃，伸向明亮却够不到的东西。

abstract.en: An empty bowl first, then the wish for bread, then the word itself.
abstract.cn: 先是一只空碗，然后是对面包的渴望，最后才是这个词。

abstract.en: Every want is a small hole in the heart shaped exactly like the missing thing.
abstract.cn: 每个心愿都是心上一个小洞，形状恰好与所缺之物吻合。

examples.en: She wanted a quiet room with a view of the sea.
examples.cn: 她想要一间看得见大海的安静房间。

examples.en: For want of evidence, the case was dismissed.
examples.cn: 因证据缺乏，案件被驳回。

examples.en: Do you want anything from the shop while I'm out?
examples.cn: 我出门时，你要从店里带点什么吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「忘它」——越想要越「忘它不忘」，得不到的才最想要。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自古诺斯语 vanta（缺乏）。

root: 古诺斯语 vanta（缺乏）→ 中古英语 wanten（缺乏→渴望）。词根一般认为属日耳曼语 *wan-（缺乏、不足），与英语前缀 wan-（如 wanhope 绝望）、形容词 wan（苍白）等相关。核心演变是「缺什么就想要什么」，由「没有」生出「渴望」。

sensesIntro.en: From the empty hand outward: wishing, requiring, lacking, poverty, the list of wants, and the face on the poster.
sensesIntro.cn: 从空着的手向外铺开：渴望、要求、缺乏、贫困、心愿清单，最后到布告上的面孔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gap in the self that reaches out as a hand
core.cn: 核心意象：自我中的缺口，以伸出的手显形

branches.en: Desire named: the wish and the things wished for
branches.cn: 被命名的愿望：心愿与心愿之物

branches.en: Lack turned into requirement
branches.cn: 缺乏转为要求：需要

branches.en: The oldest fossil: plain absence
branches.cn: 最古老的化石义：单纯的没有

branches.en: Absence grown to the size of a household
branches.cn: 缺失扩及全家：贫困

branches.en: When authority lacks you, you are wanted
branches.cn: 当权力「缺」你，你便被通缉

intro.cn: 诺斯语「缺乏」词根在英语的形容词与固定短语中留下化石。

latinIntro.cn: 此词族属日耳曼与诺斯语来源，want 词族中没有拉丁同源词。

definition_zh: 战争；斗争；冲突；交战
definition_en: organized armed fighting between countries or groups, or any sustained struggle against something
core_image: 两支队伍隔着一条线：线的两边都认为自己不得不打
scene: 博物馆的旧地图上，国境线画得又粗又黑。The two nations finally made peace after fifty years of war.
sceneCN: 这里 war 是「战争」（第 1 个义项：国家间有组织的武装冲突）；句意是五十年战争之后，两国终于讲和。

pos.zh: 名词：战争；斗争；冲突；交战状态
动词：交战；进行斗争

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「战争、作战方式」，由 war 加fare（进行）构成
形容词，义为「好战的、军事的」，由 war 加 like 构成
名词，义为「武士、战士」，由旧法语词根 guerre 加施动者后缀构成
形容词，义为「交战的」，如 warring factions

senses.title: Armed fighting between nations
senses.titleCN: 战争：国家或集团间的武装冲突
senses.definition: organized armed conflict between countries, states, or large groups
senses.definitionCN: 国家、政权或大集团之间有组织的武装冲突
senses.example: The two nations finally made peace after fifty years of war.
senses.exampleCN: 五十年的战争之后，两国终于讲和。
senses.why: Old Northern French werre means to confuse, to mix forces together; fighting is confusion made organized.
senses.whyCN: 古北方法语 werre 意为使混乱、搅混；战争就是被组织起来的大混乱。

senses.title: A sustained struggle
senses.titleCN: 斗争：对某物的长期对抗
senses.definition: a sustained campaign or struggle against a problem, not necessarily with weapons
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一问题的长期抗争，不必动用武器
senses.example: Doctors declared war on the epidemic.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们向疫情宣战。
senses.why: The confusion-energy of war is borrowed for any long, committed fight.
senses.whyCN: 战争那股搅动一切的能量，被借用于任何长期而投入的抗争。

senses.title: The state of being at war
senses.titleCN: 交战状态：战争作为国家间关系
senses.definition: the period or legal condition during which enemies fight
senses.definitionCN: 敌对双方交战的时期或法律状态
senses.example: The country was still technically at war with its neighbor.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在法律上仍与其邻国处于交战状态。
senses.why: War is not only battles but the standing condition between them.
senses.whyCN: 战争不只是战役，更是战役之间持续着的敌对状态。

senses.title: Conflict within a country
senses.titleCN: 内战：国家内部的武装冲突
senses.definition: armed conflict between groups inside one country
senses.definitionCN: 一国内部不同集团间的武装冲突
senses.example: The civil war split the region into two camps.
senses.exampleCN: 内战把这一地区分裂成两大阵营。
senses.why: When confusion turns inward, a nation fights itself with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 当混乱转向内部，国家便用同一个词与自己作战。

senses.title: Personal inner conflict
senses.titleCN: 内心交战：自我之间的拉扯
senses.definition: a conflict of feelings, duties, or thoughts inside one person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人内心情感、责任或思绪之间的冲突
senses.example: She felt at war with herself over the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个决定上，她内心天人交战。
senses.why: The battlefield shrinks to one chest; armies become feelings.
senses.whyCN: 战场缩小到一副胸腔，军队变成了情绪。

intro.en: War comes from Old Northern French werre, a variant of guerre, from Frankish *werra, meaning confusion or strife.
intro.cn: war 源自古北方法语 werre（guerre 的变体），上溯至法兰克语 *werra，意为混乱、争斗。

items.en: The reconstructed Frankish word *werra means confusion, tumult, or strife; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 重构的法兰克语 *werra 意为混乱、骚乱、争斗；其更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Guerre means war; the northern dialects keep the w- sound as werre.
items.cn: 古法语 guerre 意为战争；北方方言保留 w- 音作 werre。

items.en: English borrows werre from Norman French, displacing older words for battle.
items.cn: 12 至 13 世纪，英语借入诺曼法语的 werre，取代了更古老的「战斗」词。

items.en: War and guerre-family words settle: warrior, warfare, and warden all arrive from the same root.
items.cn: 14 至 15 世纪，guerre 词族的词定型：warrior、warfare、warden 均出自同一词根。

items.en: Metaphorical wars multiply: wars on poverty, disease, and vice in political speech.
items.cn: 16 至 19 世纪，比喻性战争增多：政治语言中出现向贫困、疾病、恶习宣战。

items.en: War now names armed conflict, trade wars, civil wars, and wars inside the self.
items.cn: 如今 war 指武装冲突、贸易战、内战与内心的交战。

note.en: War belongs to the Frankish confusion-family and the conflict word-field; look-alikes share the root or sound, near meanings share the field of fighting.
note.cn: war 属法兰克语「混乱」词族及「冲突」义场：形近组共享词根或音形，近义组共享「交战」义场。

entries.definition: a fighter, especially in earlier times
entries.definitionCN: 武士、战士；与 war 同出法语 guerre 词族

entries.definition: a person under guard; a hospital room; to guard
entries.definitionCN: 受监护人、病房、看守；与 war 同音易混，但词源为古英语 weard，不同

entries.definitionCN: 穿、磨损；发音接近 war 易混，词源不同

entries.definitionCN: 游击队员；西班牙语对 guerre 词根的小称形式

entries.definition: a single fight between armed forces
entries.definitionCN: 战役、战斗；war 是整体，battle 是其中一战

entries.definition: serious disagreement or fighting
entries.definitionCN: 冲突；兼指武力与意见之争

entries.definition: fighting between enemies
entries.definitionCN: 战斗、搏斗；强调交手的动作

entries.definition: a hard fight or effort against difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 抗争、奋斗；不必涉及武力

entries.definition: a state without war or fighting
entries.definitionCN: 和平；与本词构成正反对照

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Frankish confusion-root and its French descendants.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自法兰克语「混乱」词根及其法语后裔。

normal.en: the root *werra means confusion; war is organized confusion.
normal.cn: 词根 *werra 意为混乱；战争就是被组织起来的混乱。

normal.en: warrior and warden both keep the old guerre-root.
normal.cn: warrior（武士）与 warden（看守）都保留古老的 guerre 词根。

normal.en: guerrilla is the Spanish diminutive of the same root: little war.
normal.cn: guerrilla（游击队）是同一词根的西班牙语小称：小战争。

normal.en: ward sounds like war but comes from Old English weard, to guard.
normal.cn: ward 与 war 同音，但源自古英语 weard（看守），注意区分。

normal.en: declare war and at war with are the two fixed frames to learn first.
normal.cn: declare war 与 at war with 是最先要掌握的两个固定搭配。

abstract.en: Two rivers of people run into each other and everything mixes into noise.
abstract.cn: 两股人流相撞，一切都搅作一片喧嚣。

abstract.en: A line drawn on a map is thin, but crossing it makes thunder.
abstract.cn: 地图上的一条细线，跨过去便是雷霆。

abstract.en: Inside one chest, two small armies argue all night without a shot.
abstract.cn: 一副胸腔里，两支小军队彻夜争执，却一枪未发。

examples.en: The treaty ended a war that had lasted a generation.
examples.cn: 这项条约结束了延续一代人之久的战争。

examples.en: The two companies are waging a price war in the phone market.
examples.cn: 两家公司正在手机市场打价格战。

examples.en: He returned from the war with stories he rarely told.
examples.cn: 他从战场归来，带着很少对人讲述的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我儿」——战报传来，母亲念着「我儿在前线」，war 就是最让人揪心的那个词。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自法兰克语 *werra（混乱、争斗）。

root: 法兰克语 *werra（混乱、争斗，更早来源不确定）→ 古法语 guerre → 古北方法语 werre → 中古英语 werre/warre → 现代英语 war。同族词 warrior（武士）、warfare（作战）、guerrilla（西班牙语小称「小战争」）、warden（看守，词义另移）。核心意象是「被搅乱的大混乱」。

sensesIntro.en: From organized confusion outward: nations fighting, struggles on problems, the standing state of war, splits within one land, and the war inside one chest.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被组织的混乱向外铺开：国家交战、对问题的抗争、持续的交战状态、一国内部的分裂，最后到胸腔里的战争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two forces thrown together until everything is mixed and loud
core.cn: 核心意象：两股力量被搅在一起，直到万物混作一片喧嚣

branches.en: War between states: the battles and the standing condition
branches.cn: 国家之间的战争：战役与持续的交战状态

branches.en: The borrowed energy: long struggles without weapons
branches.cn: 被借用的能量：不动武器的长期抗争

branches.en: The confusion turned inward onto one land
branches.cn: 混乱转向内部：一国之内的冲突

branches.en: The battlefield shrunk to a single heart
branches.cn: 缩小到一颗心的战场

branches.en: Every war, outer or inner, ends in a peace that must be made
branches.cn: 每场战争——外在或内心——都以必须缔结的和平告终

latinIntro.cn: 此词族经法语进入英语，war 词族中没有拉丁同源词。

senses.title: A hospital room for patients
senses.titleCN: 病房：医院里收治病人之处
senses.definition: a large room in a hospital with beds for several patients
senses.definitionCN: 医院里放有多张病床、收容数位病人的大房间
senses.example: The nurse checked every bed in the children's ward before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜前，护士查看了儿科病房的每一张床。
senses.why: Old English weard means guard; the room is where patients are watched over.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 weard 意为看守；病房正是被看护之人所居之处。

senses.title: A person under protection
senses.titleCN: 受监护人：处于他人照管之下的人
senses.definition: a person, especially a child, placed under the care of a guardian or court
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指处于监护人或法院照管之下的孩子
senses.example: The lawyer became the ward of her young nephew.
senses.exampleCN: 律师成了年幼侄子的监护人（侄子成了她的受监护人）。
senses.why: The one kept under watch is the ward; guarding names the guarded.
senses.whyCN: 被看守之人即 ward，「守护」转而指称被守护者。

senses.title: A district of a city
senses.titleCN: 行政区：城市划分的选区
senses.definition: a division of a city for elections or administration
senses.definitionCN: 城市为选举或管理而划分的区域
senses.example: She represents the seventh ward on the city council.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市议会中代表第七选区。
senses.why: A guarded and administered piece of the city becomes a district.
senses.whyCN: 城市中被看守与管辖的一块地方，便成了一区。

senses.title: To keep away; defend against
senses.titleCN: 挡开：防避、抵御
senses.definition: to turn aside or prevent something harmful, as in ward off
senses.definitionCN: 使有害之物偏向、无法近身，如 ward off
senses.example: Vitamin C cannot really ward off every cold.
senses.exampleCN: 维生素 C 并不能真正挡住每一次感冒。
senses.why: The guard's act itself becomes a verb: to ward is to stand watch and push harm aside.
senses.whyCN: 看守的动作本身化为动词：ward 就是站岗并把伤害挡开。

senses.title: A section of a prison
senses.titleCN: 监区：监狱内分隔的区段
senses.definition: a division of a prison where prisoners are kept
senses.definitionCN: 监狱内关押囚犯的分区
senses.example: The new wing added three secure wards.
senses.exampleCN: 新楼增建了三个戒备监区。
senses.why: Where guards watch prisoners, the watched place takes the guard's name.
senses.whyCN: 看守监视囚犯之处，被看守的地方便取了看守之名。

intro.en: Ward comes from Old English weard, a watch or guard, from the Germanic root behind guard-words like watch and warden.
intro.cn: ward 源自古英语 weard（看守、守卫），出自日耳曼词根，与 watch、warden 等看守类词同源。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ward- or *war- means to watch over, keep, or guard.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ward- 或 *war- 意为看护、保管、守卫。

items.en: Weard means a watch, a keeper, or a guarding; it stands beside the French-derived guard.
items.cn: 古英语 weard 意为看守、看守者、守卫；与法语来源的 guard 并立。

items.en: Germanic *ward- also entered French, returning as guard, garde, and warder words.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 *ward- 亦借入法语，以 guard、garde、warder 等形式回流。

items.en: Ward covers guarding, the person guarded, and the act of keeping harm away.
items.cn: 中古英语 ward 兼指看守、被看守者及挡开伤害的行为。

items.en: The hospital sense grows: rooms where patients are watched become wards.
items.cn: 16 至 17 世纪，「病房」义生长：看护病人的房间成为 ward。

items.en: Ward now spans hospital rooms, city districts, wards of court, and warding off harm.
items.cn: 如今 ward 涵盖病房、行政区、受监护人与挡开危险。

note.en: Ward sits at the center of the Germanic guarding family, facing its French double guard; look-alikes share the root, near meanings share the field of watching and protecting.
note.cn: ward 处于日耳曼「看守」词族中心，与法语孪生词 guard 相对：形近组共享词根，近义组共享看护义场。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the Germanic guard-root and its French doublet guard.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自日耳曼「看守」词根及其法语孪生词 guard。

normal.en: the root means to guard; a ward is a person or place under watch.
normal.cn: 词根意为看守；ward 就是被看守的人或地方。

normal.en: guard and ward are twins: Germanic ward- dressed in French came back as guard.
normal.cn: guard 与 ward 是孪生：日耳曼 ward- 换上法语衣装回流成 guard。

normal.en: ward off keeps the verb sense: push harm aside like a guard.
normal.cn: ward off 保留动词义：像守卫一样把伤害挡开。

normal.en: warden and wardrobe both wear the same old root.
normal.cn: warden 与 wardrobe 都穿着同一古老词根。

normal.en: award is a- plus a related root: what guarding judgment hands over.
normal.cn: award 是 a- 加同根词：看守般的裁断所交出之物。

abstract.en: A lamp burns all night at one door, and behind it someone sleeps unafraid.
abstract.cn: 一盏灯彻夜守在一扇门前，门后有人安睡无惧。

abstract.en: A raised forearm deflects the blow just enough; the guard is the gesture.
abstract.cn: 抬起的小臂恰好把来击挡偏，守护本身就是那个动作。

abstract.en: A city cut into pieces, each piece with its own keeper and its own lamp.
abstract.cn: 城市被切成若干片，每片都有自己的守夜人和灯。

examples.en: The patient was moved from intensive care to a general ward.
examples.cn: 病人从重症监护室转到了普通病房。

examples.en: She raised her arm to ward off the branches.
examples.cn: 她抬起手臂挡开树枝。

examples.en: As a ward of the court, the boy lived with a foster family.
examples.cn: 作为法院监管的孩子，男孩寄住在一个寄养家庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我德（守德）」——「我守德行，也守着你。」ward 的本义就是守。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自古英语 weard（看守）。

root: 日耳曼语词根 *ward-（看守、守护）→ 古英语 weard（看守、守卫）→ 中古英语 ward。同一词根经法语回流形成 guard、garde，构成孪生词。同族词有 warden（典狱长）、warder（狱吏）、wardrobe（衣柜，字面「守衣之处」）、award（授予）、warden 等；另与 watch 同属守卫词族。

sensesIntro.en: From the guarded door outward: watched rooms, watched people, guarded city pieces, the act of warding off, and the watched section of a prison.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被守卫的门向外铺开：被看护的房间、被监护的人、被管辖的城市片区、挡开的动作，最后到监狱中被看守的监区。

branches.en: Places kept under watch: hospital room and prison section
branches.cn: 被看守之所：病房与监区

branches.en: People kept under watch: the ward of a guardian
branches.cn: 被看守之人：监护之下的 ward

branches.en: The keeper's act: turning harm aside
branches.cn: 看守的动作：把伤害挡开

branches.en: The guarded piece of the city: ward and district
branches.cn: 城市中被看守的一片：行政区

branches.en: Guarding is watching with hands ready to push away
branches.cn: 守护就是睁着眼、随时能把危险推开

intro.en: The Germanic guard-root builds keepers, places, and the act itself across ward, warden, and wardrobe.
intro.cn: 日耳曼看守词根贯穿 ward、warden、wardrobe，构成看守者、被看守之所与动作本身。

latinIntro.en: This family is Germanic, though it returned into English partly through French dress.
latinIntro.cn: 此词族属日耳曼来源，部分词形经法语衣着回流英语。

senses.title: A cabinet for clothes
senses.titleCN: 衣柜：挂放衣物的立柜
senses.definition: a tall piece of furniture with doors, used for hanging and storing clothes
senses.definitionCN: 带柜门的高大家具，用于悬挂和存放衣物
senses.example: The old wardrobe creaked whenever its door opened.
senses.exampleCN: 那口旧衣柜的门一开就吱呀作响。
senses.why: Old French warderobe means a guarded robe place: the room where robes were kept under watch.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 warderobe 意为「守衣之处」：即被看守存放长袍的房间。

senses.title: All the clothes a person has
senses.titleCN: 全部服装：一个人的整套衣装
senses.definition: the collection of clothes owned by a person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人拥有的所有衣服的总称
senses.example: She packed the whole wardrobe into two suitcases when she moved abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 出国时她把整套衣物装进了两只行李箱。
senses.why: The guarded room holds every robe; the place's contents become the person's clothes.
senses.whyCN: 守衣之屋装着所有长袍，这个地方的藏品便成了一个人的全部衣装。

senses.title: Theatrical costumes

senses.definition: the costumes of a theater or film production, or the department that keeps them

senses.example: The wardrobe team stitched the king's cloak overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 服装部连夜缝好了国王的斗篷。
senses.why: The room that once kept nobles' robes now keeps actors' costumes.
senses.whyCN: 昔日存放贵族长袍的房间，如今保管演员的戏服。

senses.title: Costumes of a period or role

senses.definition: the set of clothes appropriate to a period, activity, or role

senses.example: His winter wardrobe is mostly grey wool.
senses.exampleCN: 他的冬季行头大多是灰色呢料。
senses.why: One guarded room per need: each season and role keeps its own robes.
senses.whyCN: 每种需求各有自己的守衣之屋：每个季节、每个角色都存着自己的行头。

intro.en: Wardrobe comes from Old French warderobe or garderobe, literally a place where robes are guarded, from Germanic warder, to guard, plus robe.
intro.cn: wardrobe 源自古法语 warderobe 或 garderobe，字面为「看守长袍之处」，由日耳曼语 warder（看守）加 robe（长袍）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ward- means to guard or watch over.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ward- 意为看守、守卫。

items.en: Warderobe and garderobe name both the guarded room for robes and the robes themselves.
items.cn: 古法语 warderobe、garderobe 兼指存放长袍的守卫室与这些长袍。

items.en: Middle English borrows wardrobe first as the room where robes were stored, often near the king's chamber.
items.cn: 14 世纪，中古英语借入 wardrobe，先指存放长袍的房间，常设在王室寝殿附近。

items.en: The sense narrows to the standing cabinet for clothes in ordinary houses.
items.cn: 15 至 17 世纪，词义收窄为普通民居中存放衣物的立柜。

items.en: The collective sense grows: a person's wardrobe becomes all the clothes they own.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，集合义生长：一个人的 wardrobe 成为其全部衣装。

items.en: Wardrobe now spans furniture, clothes collections, and theatrical costume departments.
items.cn: 如今 wardrobe 涵盖家具、衣装总集与剧场服装部门。

note.en: Wardrobe stands inside the Germanic guard-family joined to French robe; look-alikes share the guard-root, near meanings share the field of storing and clothing.
note.cn: wardrobe 处于日耳曼「守护」词根与法语 robe 的结合处：形近组共享词根，近义组共享「储物与衣着」义场。

normalIntro.en: Five anchors from the guard-root warder and the French robe.
normalIntro.cn: 五个锚点，来自「守护」词根 warder 与法语 robe（长袍）。

normal.en: warder means guard; a wardrobe is literally a guarded robe place.
normal.cn: warder 意为看守；wardrobe 字面就是「被看守的长袍之处」。

normal.en: ward and wardrobe share the same Germanic guard-root.
normal.cn: ward 与 wardrobe 共享同一日耳曼守护词根。

normal.en: garderobe is the French twin with g instead of w.
normal.cn: garderobe 是法语孪生词，把 w 换成 g。

normal.en: robe itself means a long garment, and it still lives in English.
normal.cn: robe 本义为长袍，在英语中至今沿用。

normal.cn: capsule wardrobe（极简衣橱）是现代固定说法，指一小组百搭衣物。

abstract.en: A tall door opens and a whole season of mornings hangs inside.
abstract.cn: 高高的柜门打开，一整个季节的清晨挂在里面。

abstract.en: A guard stands in a small stone room where kings' robes rest, folded and counted.
abstract.cn: 小石室里站着卫兵，国王的长袍叠好存放在此，一一清点。

abstract.en: Every person owns one invisible room where all their clothes live together.
abstract.cn: 每人心里都有一间看不见的房间，所有的衣服在那里同住。

examples.en: A wardrobe stood against the wall of the small bedroom.
examples.cn: 小卧室的墙边立着一口衣柜。

examples.en: A capsule wardrobe of ten pieces can cover every occasion.
examples.cn: 十件单品组成的极简衣橱就能应对各种场合。

examples.en: Backstage, the wardrobe crew was still sewing sequins onto the dresses.
examples.cn: 后台，服装组的成员还在往裙子上缝亮片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我捉漏」——衣柜门没关严，风一吹衣架「捉漏捉漏」地晃。谐音只是记忆钩子，词源仍来自古法语 warderobe（守衣之处）。

root: 日耳曼语词根 *ward-（看守）→ 法语动词 warder（看守）+ robe（长袍）构成古法语 warderobe（守衣之处）→ 中古英语 wardrobe（存衣房间→立柜→全部衣装）。garderobe 是其法语孪生形式。robe 继续生活于英语 robe（长袍、浴袍）。核心意象是「被看护的衣装」。

sensesIntro.en: From the guarded robe-room outward: the cabinet, the whole collection of clothes, theatrical costumes, and the set for one season or role.
sensesIntro.cn: 从守衣之屋向外铺开：立柜、全部衣装、剧场戏服，最后到某季某角色的整套行头。

branches.en: The room hardened into furniture: the cabinet itself
branches.cn: 房间凝固为家具：立柜本身

branches.en: The contents become the person's whole clothing

branches.en: The guarded room now serves the stage
branches.cn: 守衣之屋如今为舞台服务

branches.en: One room per need: seasons and roles keep their own robes
branches.cn: 每种需求一间屋：季节与角色各存其衣

branches.en: From kings' robes to actors' cloaks, the keeper stays the same
branches.cn: 从国王的长袍到演员的斗篷，看守始终未变
